Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the FINRA disclosure content standard across variable annuity and variable life forms, statements and correspondence; escalates wording disputes to Regulatory Counsel and the registered principal

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - FINRA Rule 2210(d)(8) (BrokerCheck reference and hyperlink on retail-facing webpages and registered-person profiles), FINRA Rule 2210(d)(1) content standards and FINRA Rule 4513 (records of written customer complaints) re-read on the FINRA Rulebook at each form-change cycle, together with any Regulatory Notice amending them

In-scope processes.value: Form and correspondence change intake for variable annuity and variable insurance products: new/revised applications, prospectus wrappers, confirms, quarterly statements, welcome kits, service letters, contact-centre email templates, rep profile webpages and the public website

In-scope systems.value: Form inventory and approved-template library holding every customer-facing artifact with its disclosure status; feeds the Policy Administration Platform print streams and the public website rep-profile pages

Compliance procedure documented.value: Disclosure Build Procedure for FINRA-regulated communications - inventory, obligation-to-artifact mapping, standard complaint/BrokerCheck disclosure block, principal approval, template load, rendered-output QA, AREF filing where required

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the registered principal designated under Rule 2210(b)(1); re-approved on any FINRA Regulatory Notice touching Rule 2210 and at least annually

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per change - retail communications concerning variable products filed with FINRA Advertising Regulation within 10 business days of first use (or 10 business days prior to first use for pre-use categories); disclosure block must be live in production before the first customer send of the changed artifact

Deadline reminders configured.value: Form inventory workflow alerts at T-20, T-10 and T-3 business days to the artifact go-live date, plus an AREF filing-due alert fired on the recorded first-use date of every retail communication

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Form inventory snapshot, principal approval, rendered proof PDF and AREF filing acknowledgement retained 3 years from last use per SEA Rule 17a-4(b)(4); written complaint files retained 4 years per FINRA Rule 4513

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any artifact sent to customers without the complaint-channel and BrokerCheck disclosure, or any retail communication used without its AREF filing, is logged as a compliance exception with the send volume, root cause, corrective mailing decision and closure date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off every disclosure wording change and every remediation plan where non-conforming artifacts already reached customers

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All customer-facing forms, statements and correspondence templates in the form inventory that were created or amended during the period, plus every public webpage intended for retail investors and every registered-person profile page

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on the mandatory elements - a sampled artifact missing the complaint-filing instructions, the firm contact details, the FINRA contact details or the BrokerCheck reference/hyperlink is a fail; any fail with customer sends already made escalates to the Head of Compliance within one business day

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per change; testing runs each quarter over that quarter's changed artifacts and re-sweeps 100% of retail-facing webpages and rep profile pages annually

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly disclosure-content test workpaper (inventory extract, sample list, rendered proofs, webpage captures, exception log) filed in the compliance evidence repository under REG-014-C01

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Form inventory export showing disclosure status per artifact, principal approval records, AREF submission numbers and complaint routing statistics, assemblable for a FINRA cycle exam Rule 2210/4513 request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance owns the FINRA exam or Advertising Regulation comment-letter response; Regulatory Counsel clears any response that concedes a non-conforming communication reached retail investors

checklist.step: Build the master inventory of customer-facing artifacts
actions: In the document management repository open the Forms library and filter Product Line = Variable Annuity / Variable Life and Audience = Customer to list every application, contract page, rider, confirm, statement, welcome kit and service letter.
Ask the Contact Center Ops Manager for the current export of outbound email and letter templates from the service desk and add each template as its own inventory row.
Ask the Digital Channel Manager for the sitemap of pages intended for retail investors and every registered-person profile page and add them as rows tagged WEB.
Record on each row: artifact id, form number and edition date, owning team, delivery channel (print, email, web, portal), annual send volume and last revision date.
Publish the inventory as the single form inventory of record and lock edit rights to the Policy Forms Specialist and Marketing Compliance Analyst.
checklist.done: every customer-facing artifact, template and retail webpage appears once in the form inventory with channel, volume and edition date.

checklist.step: Map each FINRA disclosure obligation to the artifacts that must carry it
actions: In the Internal Regulatory System open REG-014 and read the obligation text for Rule 2210(d)(8), Rule 2210(d)(1) and Rule 4513.

Add a column to the form inventory for each required element: complaint-filing instructions, firm name and complaints mailing address, firm complaints telephone number and email, FINRA telephone number and finra.org address, BrokerCheck reference and hyperlink.
Set each cell to REQUIRED or NOT APPLICABLE and, where NOT APPLICABLE, type the reason (for example internal-use-only material or institutional communication under Rule 2210(a)(3)).
Mark every page that is an initial retail webpage or carries a professional profile of a registered person as REQUIRED for the BrokerCheck reference and hyperlink.
Send the mapped inventory to the Head of Compliance for confirmation before drafting begins.
checklist.done: each inventory row shows, element by element, whether the disclosure is required and why.

checklist.step: Draft the standard complaint-channel and FINRA contact disclosure block
actions: Draft one reusable block containing: how to file a complaint with the firm (mailing address, telephone, email, web form URL), the statement that complaints may also be directed to FINRA, FINRA's public telephone number and finra.org, and the BrokerCheck reference with its hyperlink.
Draft a print variant that spells out the BrokerCheck URL in full because a hyperlink cannot be clicked on paper.
Check the block against Rule 2210(d)(1) content standards: no promissory or exaggerated wording, balanced presentation, no omission of material qualifications.
Have the Content Specialist set the block to a minimum 9-point body size and confirm the colour contrast is legible in the statement and confirm templates.
Circulate the draft to the Complaints Manager to confirm every listed channel is one the complaints function actually monitors.
checklist.done: a print variant and a digital variant of the disclosure block exist, each naming only monitored complaint channels.

checklist.step: Place the BrokerCheck reference and hyperlink on retail webpages and rep profiles
actions: In the portal content management screens open each page tagged WEB in the inventory and insert the BrokerCheck reference into the page footer component so it renders above the fold on mobile as well as desktop.

Point the hyperlink at the BrokerCheck landing page and, on registered-person profile pages, at that individual's BrokerCheck record keyed on their CRD number supplied by the Producer Licensing Coordinator.
Confirm the reference is readily apparent - not collapsed behind a Legal accordion, not rendered only in an image, and reachable by screen reader.
Run the site link checker across every changed page and fix any 404 or redirect before publishing.
Capture a dated screenshot of each published page into the form inventory row as the placement evidence.
checklist.done: every initial retail webpage and every registered-person profile carries a working, readily apparent BrokerCheck reference and hyperlink, evidenced by a dated capture.

checklist.step: Obtain registered principal and counsel approval of the wording
actions: Read the draft block against the current text of FINRA Rules 2210(d)(1), 2210(d)(8), 2211 and 4513 on the FINRA Rulebook and note any Regulatory Notice issued since the last approval.
Confirm the complaint instructions do not discourage a customer from contacting FINRA or condition escalation on exhausting the firm's process.
Return line-level edits to the Marketing Compliance Analyst and re-read the revised block rather than approving in principle.
Have the registered principal designated under Rule 2210(b)(1) sign and date the approval on the final wording, naming the artifacts it covers.
File the signed approval in the compliance evidence repository under the change id.
checklist.done: a dated principal approval and counsel clearance exist for the exact final wording, listing the artifacts covered.

checklist.step: Load the approved block into the correspondence template library
actions: In the template library open each affected template, insert the approved block as a shared content fragment rather than pasted text so future wording changes propagate once.
Bind the fragment variables (firm complaints address, telephone, email, web form URL) to reference data so a channel change does not require editing every template.
Increment each template version, enter the change id in the version comment and set the effective date to the agreed go-live.
Hand the changed template list to the QA Analyst and the Policy Administration Analyst for downstream rendering.
checklist.done: every affected template references the single approved fragment and carries a new version number tied to the change id.

checklist.step: Configure the statement, confirm and service-letter print streams to carry the block
actions: In the policy administration correspondence configuration open the variable annuity quarterly statement, transaction confirm and service-letter document definitions.
Attach the new template versions and set the effective date so the next scheduled statement cycle picks them up.
Check the page-break rules so the disclosure block cannot be orphaned onto a page that is suppressed for duplex printing.
Run a print-stream simulation for 20 sample contracts covering single and joint owners, and pull the generated PDFs for review.
Confirm with the print vendor coordinator that the changed stock and page count stay inside the existing envelope specification.
checklist.done: simulated statements, confirms and service letters all render the disclosure block in full on a non-suppressed page.

checklist.step: Wire every advertised complaint channel into the complaints queue
actions: For each channel named in the disclosure block (mailing address, telephone number, email box, web form) create or confirm an intake route that opens a case in the complaints queue.

Set the case type to Written Customer Complaint where the contact arrives in writing so it lands in the Rule 4513 file, and set the office of supervisory jurisdiction from the servicing rep's assigned OSJ.
Configure mandatory capture fields: complainant name, contract number, date received, product, nature of complaint, associated person named, and the FINRA problem and product codes.
Set the acknowledgement SLA and the escalation rule that routes any complaint naming a registered person to the Head of Compliance the same business day.
Send a test contact through each channel and confirm a case is created with the right type and OSJ.
checklist.done: each advertised channel produces a correctly typed, correctly routed complaint case in a live end-to-end test.

checklist.step: Publish the routing rules and contact matrix to the contact centre
actions: Load the new complaint-handling knowledge article with the exact firm and FINRA contact details agents must give when asked how to complain.
Add a disposition code for Complaint - Written and Complaint - Oral so agents cannot close a complaint contact as a general enquiry.
Configure the screen-pop prompt that instructs the agent to log the contact in the complaints queue when the customer expresses dissatisfaction in writing.
Brief the supervisors that agents must never offer to resolve a matter in exchange for the customer not contacting FINRA.
checklist.done: agents have the published contact matrix, the complaint disposition codes are live and supervisors have been briefed.

checklist.step: File the changed retail communications with FINRA Advertising Regulation
actions: Classify every changed artifact as retail communication, correspondence or institutional communication under Rule 2210(a) and record the classification on the inventory row.

For retail communications concerning variable products, submit the piece through the FINRA Advertising Regulation Electronic Filing system with the filing type, first-use date, and the principal approval attached.
Observe the deadline: file within 10 business days of first use, or 10 business days prior to first use for the categories that require pre-use filing.
Record the AREF submission number and submission date on the inventory row and diary the expected comment-letter window.
Where a comment letter arrives, log it as an issue, make the requested amendment and re-file the amended piece before further use.
checklist.done: every filing-eligible retail communication has an AREF submission number recorded against its inventory row within the applicable 10-business-day window.

checklist.step: Stamp disclosure status onto the version-controlled inventory
actions: Set each inventory row to COMPLIANT, PENDING or EXEMPT and record the template version, approval date, principal name and AREF submission number that support the status.
Freeze a dated snapshot of the inventory at each go-live so the state of the estate on any past date can be reproduced.
Flag every row still PENDING within 5 business days of go-live and escalate to the Head of Compliance.
Retire superseded template versions to a read-only archive rather than deleting them.
checklist.done: a dated inventory snapshot exists at go-live with a supported status on every row and no unexplained PENDING rows.

checklist.step: QA the rendered output before customers see it
actions: Render one live-data proof per changed artifact in each channel (print PDF, HTML email, portal view) rather than testing the template in isolation.
Check element by element that the complaint instructions, firm contact details, FINRA contact details and BrokerCheck reference are present, legible and not truncated.
Click every hyperlink in the email and portal proofs and confirm it resolves to the intended destination over HTTPS.
Test the email proof in the three highest-volume mail clients to confirm the block is not stripped by the plain-text fallback.
Log any failure as a release blocker in the change record and re-test after the fix.
checklist.done: a signed proof pack exists showing every changed artifact rendering all required elements in every delivery channel.

checklist.step: Align the Rule 4513 complaint file at each office of supervisory jurisdiction
actions: Create or confirm a complaint file per office of supervisory jurisdiction holding each written customer complaint and the action taken by the firm.
Set the retention label to 4 years per FINRA Rule 4513 and confirm the record is retrievable by OSJ, complainant, associated person and receipt date.
Reconcile the complaints queue export to the OSJ files for the last full month and open a gap item for anything present in one and missing from the other.
Confirm the file is accessible to the examiners on request at the OSJ location as well as centrally.
checklist.done: every OSJ has a 4-year-retained complaint file that reconciles to the complaints queue for the last full month.

checklist.step: Train front-line and supervisory staff on the changed disclosure and routing
actions: Build a short course covering what changed, where the disclosure now appears, the exact FINRA contact details and the rule that a written expression of dissatisfaction is a complaint.
Assign the course in the learning management system to contact-centre agents, service representatives, registered persons selling variable products and their supervising principals.
Set a 15-business-day completion window from the artifact go-live date and enable manager escalation on non-completion.
Export the completion report at the deadline and give the outstanding list to the relevant supervising principals.
checklist.done: the course is assigned to every affected population and the completion report plus outstanding list is filed.

checklist.step: File the evidence pack for the change
actions: Assemble the pack: inventory snapshot, obligation mapping, approved wording with principal signature and counsel clearance, rendered proofs, webpage captures, AREF acknowledgements, complaint-routing test results and the training completion report.
File it under REG-014-C01 with the change id and go-live date in the folder name.
Apply the retention labels: 3 years from last use for communications evidence, 4 years for complaint records.
Confirm the repository index makes the pack searchable by form number, template version and AREF submission number.
checklist.done: the complete evidence pack is filed, retention-labelled and searchable by form number and AREF submission number.

testing.step: Build the population of artifacts changed or in use during the period
actions: Extract every form inventory row with a template version effective inside the period, plus every row tagged WEB regardless of change date.
Add the outbound correspondence template export from the contact centre and the print vendor's list of document types actually produced in the period so artifacts outside the inventory cannot hide.
Reconcile the inventory count to the print vendor's produced-document types and the portal sitemap; investigate and resolve every difference before sampling.
Sign the population as complete, recording the extract date, row count and the reconciling items.
testing.done: the population reconciles to print vendor output and the live sitemap and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the inventory to what customers actually received
actions: Pull the correspondence history for the period from policy administration by document type and count sends per template version.
Match each sent template version to an inventory row with a COMPLIANT status effective on or before the send date.
List any template version sent to customers with no inventory row, or with a status of PENDING at the send date, as an automatic exception with the send volume attached.
Confirm no retired template version was still in production use after its retirement date.
testing.done: every template version sent in the period matches an inventory row that was COMPLIANT at the send date, or is listed as an exception with volume.

testing.step: Draw and document a reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of retail-facing webpages and registered-person profile pages.
Take 100% of the five highest-volume customer artifacts by send count.
Take 25 further artifacts selected at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population, for a minimum of 40 items overall.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn independently.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible from the recorded seed and covers all web pages and the top five volume artifacts.

testing.step: Re-perform the disclosure content check on a live rendered copy
actions: Obtain, for each sampled artifact, a copy as the customer received it - a production print image, a delivered email, or the live page - not a template screenshot.
Tick element by element: complaint-filing instructions, firm complaints address, firm telephone and email, FINRA telephone and finra.org, BrokerCheck reference and hyperlink.
Reach the conclusion before opening the inventory status, then compare; a COMPLIANT status on an artifact missing an element is an exception on both the artifact and the control.
Attach the annotated rendered copy to the workpaper as the evidence of re-performance.
testing.done: each sampled artifact has an independent element-by-element re-performance note with the annotated customer copy attached.

testing.step: Test the BrokerCheck reference and hyperlink on the live site
actions: Open each sampled retail webpage and rep profile in a clean browser session on both desktop and mobile viewports.
Confirm the reference is readily apparent without expanding an accordion and that the hyperlink resolves to BrokerCheck rather than a redirect or an error page.
On rep profile pages, confirm the link lands on that individual's record and that the CRD number matches the roster supplied by the Producer Licensing Coordinator.
Capture the URL, the timestamp and a screenshot of each tested page into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled page shows a working, readily apparent BrokerCheck link resolving to the correct record, evidenced by timestamped captures.

testing.step: Verify the complaint channels advertised are the channels monitored
actions: Take the exact address, telephone number, email box and web form URL printed on each sampled artifact.
Send a controlled test contact into each channel, marked as a test, and confirm a complaint case is opened with the correct case type, OSJ and mandatory fields.
Compare the advertised channel list to the intake routes configured in the case tool and list any advertised channel with no route as a fail.
Record the case numbers created by the test contacts in the workpaper and close them as test records.
testing.done: every advertised channel produced a correctly typed complaint case in a controlled test, with case numbers recorded.

testing.step: Trace sampled retail communications to their FINRA filing and approval
actions: For each sampled retail communication, locate the recorded AREF submission number and open the submission record and its acknowledgement.
Confirm the filed piece is the version in use by comparing the filed attachment to the rendered customer copy page for page.
Confirm a dated registered principal approval exists and pre-dates the first-use date on the record.
Where a comment letter was received, confirm the amendment was made and the amended piece re-filed before further use.
testing.done: each sampled retail communication traces to a matching filed version, a pre-dated principal approval and a closed comment letter where one exists.

testing.step: Recompute the filing clock and the go-live gate
actions: For each filed sample item, recompute the due date as first-use date plus 10 business days using the exchange business-day calendar, excluding weekends and holidays.
Compare to the actual AREF submission date and record the days late for anything outside the window.
For pre-use categories, confirm the submission date is at least 10 business days before first use and treat any shortfall as a breach rather than an exception.
Check the first customer send date against the template version effective date to prove nothing went out on an unapproved version.
testing.done: the filing-clock recomputation reconciles for every sample item and no artifact was sent before its approved version was effective.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the artifact id, template version, missing element, channel and the number of customers who received the non-conforming version.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: inventory gap, template loaded without the shared fragment, web page published outside the CMS workflow, filing missed, channel advertised but not monitored.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and decide with Regulatory Counsel whether a corrective mailing or a website correction notice is required.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with customer impact, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate by element and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold for the mandatory elements.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references that support it.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted, approved or loaded none of the sampled artifacts, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the result and any open customer-impacting breach to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper under REG-014-C01.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate by element and a committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns generation and on-time delivery of every FINRA-driven customer notice and firm filing trigger for variable annuity and variable life business; escalates missed clocks to the Head of Compliance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - FINRA Rule 1240(b) (Firm Element delivery by December 31 each year), FINRA Rule 2210(c) (filing with Advertising Regulation within 10 business days of first use), FINRA Rule 4530(a)-(b) (report within 30 calendar days of knowledge) and Rule 4530(f) (file copies within 30 calendar days of receipt) re-read on the FINRA Rulebook at each annual procedure refresh

In-scope processes.value: Event-driven notice generation for variable products: SIPC address and telephone notice at account opening and annually, prospectus and statement of additional information delivery, transaction confirms, contract-change and rider notices, complaint acknowledgements, and the internal triggers that start the Rule 4530 30-day reporting clocks

In-scope systems.value: Notice generation engine, the correspondence history that timestamps each send, and the notice log that records trigger date, due date and actual send date per notice type

Compliance procedure documented.value: Notice Generation and Timeliness Procedure - trigger catalogue, day-count rules (calendar versus business day), suppression rules, undeliverable handling, exception queue and the escalation path for a breached clock

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Policy Admin Ops Lead; re-approved annually and on any FINRA Regulatory Notice that changes a deadline

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Rule 4530(a)/(b) reports within 30 calendar days of knowledge; Rule 4530(f) document copies within 30 calendar days of receipt; Rule 2210(c) retail communications within 10 business days of first use; Firm Element delivery completed by December 31; annual SIPC notice inside the customer's anniversary month; account-opening SIPC notice within 30 days of account establishment

Deadline reminders configured.value: Notice log timers open on the trigger date and fire at 50% of the window, at 5 days remaining and on the day of breach; the 30-calendar-day Rule 4530 clocks additionally page the Head of Compliance at day 20

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Notice log extract, generated notice image and the delivery or mail-house confirmation retained 6 years for account records and 3 years from last use for communications, per SEA Rule 17a-4

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every notice sent after its due date, suppressed in error or returned undeliverable without re-issue is logged with the day count over, the customers affected, the root cause and the corrective send date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late or missed Rule 4530 clock and every corrective mailing where a required customer notice was not delivered on time

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All notice-triggering events in the period - new variable annuity account openings, contract anniversaries, contract changes, complaint receipts, service of a civil complaint or arbitration claim, and reportable events under Rule 4530 - taken from the policy administration event log and the legal matter register

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Notice generated and sent inside the applicable window: 100% required for the 30-calendar-day Rule 4530 clocks and for annual SIPC notices; a single day late on a Rule 4530 clock is a reportable breach, and a customer-notice on-time rate below 98% fails the control

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven with an annual cycle; testing runs monthly over the prior month's notice log and a full-year sweep of the annual SIPC population each January

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Policy Administration and must not have generated, suppressed or released any sampled notice

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly notice-timeliness workpaper (event extract, notice log join, ageing calculation, sample images, exception list) filed in the compliance evidence repository under REG-014-C02

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Notice log export showing trigger date, due date, send date and days variance per notice, with sample notice images and mail-house confirmations, producible for a FINRA cycle exam request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance owns the FINRA examiner request; Regulatory Counsel clears any response disclosing a late Rule 4530 report and decides whether a late filing must be self-reported

checklist.step: Build the catalogue of FINRA-driven notice triggers and their clocks
actions: In the Internal Regulatory System open REG-014 and list every event that starts a clock: account opening, contract anniversary, contract or rider change, complaint receipt, receipt of a criminal information or indictment, service of a civil complaint or arbitration claim, and knowledge of a Rule 4530(a) reportable event.
For each trigger record the rule cite, the recipient (customer or FINRA), the window, and whether the window is counted in calendar days or business days.

Set the Rule 4530(a)/(b) and 4530(f) windows to 30 calendar days from knowledge or receipt; set the Rule 2210(c) window to 10 business days from first use; set the Firm Element completion date to December 31.
Write the day-zero rule for each trigger in words - for example, the 4530(f) clock starts on the date the document is received by any associated person, not the date it reaches Legal.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the day-zero definitions in writing before the catalogue is used to configure timers.
checklist.done: every trigger has a rule cite, recipient, window, day-count basis and a counsel-confirmed day-zero definition.

checklist.step: Map each trigger to the system event that will detect it
actions: For each catalogue trigger, name the source event: policy administration transaction code for account establishment, the anniversary batch for the annual notice, the endorsement transaction for contract change, and the complaints queue case creation for complaint receipt.

For legal triggers, agree with the Litigation Manager that service of process is registered in the legal matter register within one business day of receipt, since that entry starts the 30-calendar-day clock.
Document the field that carries the trigger date on each source event and confirm it is a system-set timestamp, not a user-typed date.
List any trigger with no reliable system event and raise it as a build item rather than accepting a manual watch.
checklist.done: each trigger names a system event and a system-set trigger-date field, with build items raised for any gap.

checklist.step: Open the notice log entry the moment a trigger fires
actions: Configure the notice log to create a row automatically on each trigger event carrying: trigger id, contract number, customer id, trigger date, notice type, rule cite, computed due date and status Open.

Compute the due date in the log from the trigger date plus the window using the correct calendar - calendar days for the 30-day Rule 4530 clocks, business days for the 10-business-day Rule 2210 clock.
Block manual editing of the trigger date and due date; corrections must be made by a supervisor with a reason code that is itself logged.
Run the log creation in parallel with the existing process for one cycle and reconcile counts before switching off the manual sheet.
checklist.done: every trigger event opens a log row automatically with a system-computed due date that no user can edit.

checklist.step: Deliver the SIPC notice at account opening and on the annual cycle
actions: Configure the new-account welcome pack to include the SIPC website address and telephone number and the statement that the customer may obtain the SIPC brochure on request, and generate it on account establishment.
Configure the annual cycle to reissue the same notice in the contract anniversary month for every open account, driven from the anniversary batch rather than a manual list.
Set the delivery channel from the customer's standing e-delivery consent, falling back to print where consent is absent or has been withdrawn.
Confirm the brochure request path - the telephone number and email box printed on the notice - is monitored by the service team and produces a fulfilment case.
Close the notice log row only when the correspondence history records a completed send.
checklist.done: every open account received the SIPC notice at opening and once in its anniversary month, with the send recorded in correspondence history.

checklist.step: Generate event-driven contract and transaction notices on time
actions: Configure the confirm generation to run on the transaction settlement date for every purchase, exchange, transfer, surrender, withdrawal and sub-account reallocation on a variable contract.
Configure contract-change and rider notices to generate on the endorsement effective date and to carry the changed values before and after.
Set the nightly batch to sweep any trigger with no generated document and place it in an exception queue rather than letting it age silently.
Have the Operations Specialist work the exception queue to zero each morning and record the reason code on any item that cannot be generated.
checklist.done: the nightly sweep leaves no ungenerated trigger older than one business day, and every exception carries a reason code.

checklist.step: Start and drive the Rule 4530(f) document-copy clock
actions: Register in the matter management system every criminal indictment or information, civil complaint and arbitration claim naming the firm or an associated person, entering the actual date of receipt.
Open a notice log row on the same day with the 30-calendar-day Rule 4530(f) due date computed from that receipt date.
Prepare the copy to be filed with FINRA and route it to the Head of Compliance for release, targeting submission by day 20 to leave buffer.
Submit the copy through the FINRA Gateway Rule 4530 application and record the submission id and date on the notice log row.
Where the document names an associated person, notify the Producer Compliance Manager so any related Form U4 disclosure amendment is assessed in parallel.
checklist.done: every registered legal document has a 4530(f) submission id recorded within 30 calendar days of the receipt date on the matter record.

checklist.step: Drive the Rule 4530(a) and (b) event reports
actions: Define knowledge date as the date the firm or an associated person first knew or should have known of the reportable event, and record it explicitly on the issue when the event is raised.
Complete the Rule 4530 report in the FINRA Gateway application selecting the correct problem and product codes for the variable product involved.
Attach the supporting documents and have Regulatory Counsel review the narrative before release, because the narrative is the record FINRA examines.
Submit within 30 calendar days of the knowledge date, record the submission id, and file the confirmation in the evidence repository.
Where the 30-day window will be missed, escalate to the Head of Compliance before the deadline rather than after it.
checklist.done: each reportable event has a knowledge date, a submitted 4530 report with its submission id, and counsel review of the narrative.

checklist.step: Handle undeliverable and returned notices
actions: Load the mail-house return file and the email bounce file daily and match each return to its notice log row.
Reopen the log row with status Undeliverable rather than leaving it closed on the original send.
Trigger address research through the servicing representative and the Broker Relationship Manager for broker-sold contracts, and re-issue within 10 business days of the return.
Where no address can be found, flag the contract for the escheatment and lost-contract process and record that outcome on the row.
checklist.done: every returned notice is reopened, researched and either re-issued within 10 business days or routed to the lost-contract process.

checklist.step: Control suppressions so a notice is never silently dropped
actions: List every suppression rule in force - do-not-mail flags, householding, e-delivery consent, litigation holds, test accounts - and record which notice types each rule may and may not suppress.
Hard-code the FINRA-required notices as non-suppressible so no marketing preference can stop them.
Require a named approver and a reason code on any manual suppression and write both to the notice log row.
Review the suppression report monthly with the Compliance Manager and reverse any suppression applied to a required notice.
checklist.done: required FINRA notices cannot be suppressed by preference rules, and every manual suppression carries an approver and reason code.

checklist.step: Run the daily ageing report and clear the at-risk queue
actions: Publish a daily ageing report from the notice log showing open rows by notice type with days elapsed and days remaining against the due date.
Split the report into Green (over half the window remaining), Amber (5 days or fewer remaining) and Red (past due).
Work the Amber queue to zero daily and escalate every Red row to the Head of Compliance the same business day with the reason it slipped.
Circulate the report each morning to Policy Administration, Compliance and Legal so the same numbers drive all three teams.
checklist.done: the ageing report is published daily, the Amber queue is cleared to zero and every Red row has a same-day escalation.

checklist.step: Reconcile the notice log to what the print and email vendors actually delivered
actions: Load the mail-house production file and the email service provider delivery file into the warehouse each day.
Join on notice id and compare generated count, sent count and delivered count by notice type and date.
Investigate any generated-but-not-sent difference the same day; a document that exists only in the archive was never delivered to the customer.
Publish the daily reconciliation with the three counts and the unresolved difference so the gap is visible rather than netted away.
checklist.done: the daily reconciliation shows generated, sent and delivered counts by notice type with every difference explained.

checklist.step: Close the annual Firm Element and December 31 deadlines
actions: In October, pull the roster of covered registered persons and the completion status of the Firm Element programme from the learning management system.
Issue individual notices to those outstanding at 60 days, 30 days and 10 days before December 31, copying their supervising principal.
Track each notice on the notice log with a December 31 due date so the annual deadline is managed with the same discipline as event clocks.
Report the outstanding population weekly through December to the Head of Compliance and apply the firm's restriction on registered activity to anyone still outstanding on January 1.
checklist.done: the December 31 population is tracked on the notice log, escalated at 60/30/10 days and closed or restricted on January 1.

checklist.step: Escalate and remediate a breached clock
actions: On any past-due row, open an issue within one business day recording the trigger date, due date, days late and the customers or filings affected.
Decide the corrective action in writing: immediate send with a cover explanation, a late Rule 4530 submission with an explanatory narrative, or a self-report to FINRA where the lateness is systemic.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear any submission that concedes lateness before it leaves the firm.
Assign the root-cause fix to a named owner with a date, and place the notice type into the next month's test as a mandatory retest.
checklist.done: every breached clock has a dated issue, a written corrective action cleared by counsel, a named root-cause owner and a retest commitment.

checklist.step: Retain the notice evidence to the required period
actions: Archive the generated notice image, the notice log row and the vendor delivery confirmation together as one retrievable record keyed on notice id.
Apply 6-year retention to account-record notices and 3-year-from-last-use retention to communications, per SEA Rule 17a-4.
Confirm records are retrievable by contract number, customer name, notice type and send date, since examiners request by contract.
Test retrieval on 10 records each quarter and record the retrieval times.
checklist.done: notice image, log row and delivery confirmation are archived as one record, retention-labelled and proven retrievable by contract number.

checklist.step: Refresh the trigger catalogue when FINRA changes a deadline
actions: Subscribe to FINRA Regulatory Notices and the Rulebook change feed and review new items weekly against the trigger catalogue.
Where a window, a form or a filing channel changes, raise a change request against the notice configuration with the effective date from the notice.
Re-run the day-zero definitions past Regulatory Counsel for any amended rule.
Version the catalogue, record the FINRA notice number that drove the change and brief Policy Administration and Legal before the effective date.
checklist.done: the catalogue carries a version, the driving FINRA notice number and a configuration change request completed before each effective date.

testing.step: Build the population of notice-triggering events for the period
actions: Extract every account establishment, contract anniversary, endorsement, surrender, withdrawal and sub-account transaction in the period from the policy administration event log.
Extract every complaint case opened in the period and every legal document registered in the matter management system.
Union the extracts into one event population keyed on trigger id, with trigger type, trigger date and contract or matter reference.
Sign the population as complete after reconciling event counts to the monthly transaction and matter volume reports.
testing.done: one reconciled event population exists covering policy, complaint and legal triggers, signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile events to notice log rows
actions: Left-join the event population to the notice log on trigger id and list every event with no log row as an automatic exception.
Check the log's trigger date equals the event's system timestamp, since a shifted trigger date silently extends the deadline.
Identify log rows with no matching event - these signal manual rows created outside the automated path - and inspect each one.
Reconcile the total row count in both directions and record the reconciling items in the workpaper.
testing.done: the event population and the notice log reconcile in both directions, with unmatched rows on either side listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample weighted to the hard deadlines
actions: Take 100% of Rule 4530(a), (b) and (f) items in the period, as these carry the 30-calendar-day statutory clocks.
Take 100% of any row that closed within two days of its due date, since near-misses show where the process is fragile.
Take 25 rows selected at random with a recorded seed from the remaining customer-notice population, minimum 40 items overall.
Record the seed, the strata, the population sizes and the draw date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample covers all Rule 4530 items and all near-miss rows and is reproducible from the recorded seed.

testing.step: Recompute every deadline from source rather than reading the log
actions: Rebuild each sampled due date from the source trigger date: add 30 calendar days for Rule 4530(a)/(b)/(f), 10 business days on the exchange holiday calendar for Rule 2210(c) filings.
Compare the recomputed date to the due date held on the log and flag any difference as a configuration exception even where the notice went out on time.
Compute days variance as actual send or submission date minus recomputed due date and record it per row.
Show the full calculation in the workpaper, including the holiday calendar used, so the maths can be re-performed.
testing.done: every sampled due date is independently recomputed, variance is stated in days and configuration differences are flagged.

testing.step: Trace the customer-notice sample to the delivered document
actions: Retrieve the archived notice image for each sampled customer notice using the notice id.

Confirm the image carries the right contract number, the right customer address of record on the send date and the required content for that notice type, including the SIPC website address and telephone number where applicable.
Match the image to a mail-house or email service delivery confirmation, since generation without delivery is not compliance.
Record the retrieval time and attach the image and confirmation to the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled customer notice traces to an archived image with correct content and a vendor delivery confirmation.

testing.step: Re-perform the Rule 4530 judgement in the regulator system
actions: For each sampled 4530 item, open the submitted report in the FINRA Gateway Rule 4530 application and read the narrative and the codes as filed.
Reach an independent view of the knowledge or receipt date from the underlying document and correspondence before looking at the date recorded by the firm.
Compare the selected problem and product codes to the event described; a right-date, wrong-code filing is still an exception.

Confirm every criminal information or indictment, civil complaint and arbitration claim in the matter register was filed under 4530(f), and identify any that were assessed as out of scope without a written basis.
testing.done: each sampled 4530 item has an independent view of the clock start date and a code-by-code comparison to the filed report.

testing.step: Test the annual SIPC notice population end to end
actions: Build the population of accounts open at any point in the year and count, per account, the SIPC notices generated at opening and in the anniversary month.
List every account with zero annual notices and every account whose notice fell outside its anniversary month.
Confirm the notice content included both the SIPC website address and telephone number and the brochure availability statement.
Reconcile the notice count to the in-force account count as at each month end and explain the difference.
testing.done: every account open in the year is shown to have received the SIPC notice at opening and within its anniversary month, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Test the suppression and undeliverable paths
actions: Extract every suppression applied in the period and confirm no FINRA-required notice type appears.
For each manual suppression, confirm an approver name and a reason code exist and that the approver was authorised.
Take the returned-mail and bounce files and confirm each return reopened its notice log row and produced a re-issue within 10 business days.
List any return closed with no re-issue and no lost-contract routing as an exception with the customer count.
testing.done: no required notice was suppressed, every manual suppression is approved with a reason and every return is re-issued or routed to the lost-contract process.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying trigger id, notice type, days late, customers or filings affected and the rule cite breached.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: trigger not detected, due date miscomputed, generation failed, delivery failed, suppression applied in error, manual queue not worked.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and record whether a corrective send or a late regulatory submission was made.
Carry every open exception into the next monthly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with days late and impact, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute on-time rate per notice type and compare to the thresholds - 100% for the 30-calendar-day Rule 4530 clocks and annual SIPC notices, 98% for the remainder.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Policy Administration and generated none of the sampled notices, sign and date the workpaper.
Report on-time rates, breached clocks and open self-report decisions to the Compliance Committee monthly and file the signed workpaper under REG-014-C02.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with on-time rates by notice type, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

In-scope processes.value: Change control over the automated controls that enforce FINRA rules: notice due-date computation, non-suppressible notice flags, principal-approval gating on communication templates, Firm Element assignment and December 31 completion enforcement, and the complaint case type that feeds the Rule 4513 file

In-scope systems.value: Correspondence and notice configuration in policy administration, plus the learning management system CE rules and the case management complaint routing; all changed only through the ITSM change record

Compliance procedure documented.value: FINRA Control Configuration Standard - the configuration baseline, the requirement-to-rule traceability matrix, mandatory compliance approval on any change touching a FINRA control, regression test pack and the post-implementation verification

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of IT and the Head of Compliance; the traceability matrix is re-approved on every FINRA Regulatory Notice affecting the cited rules and at least annually

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per change - configuration must be live before the business effective date of the rule change; annual items are hard-dated in configuration (Firm Element completion enforced at December 31) and the 30-calendar-day and 10-business-day clocks are held as parameters, not as code

Deadline reminders configured.value: Change calendar alerts at T-15, T-5 and T-1 business days to each regulatory effective date, plus an automated alert whenever a deadline parameter value is edited in any environment

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every change to a FINRA-enforcing rule and every remediation of configuration drift before the change is closed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All change records in the period that touched a system enforcing a FINRA rule, plus the full set of live configuration values for deadline parameters, non-suppressible notice flags, principal-approval gates and CE assignment rules as at the test date

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - any FINRA-enforcing change released without documented compliance approval and passing regression evidence is a fail, as is any live parameter that differs from the approved baseline; one fail escalates to the Head of Compliance and the Head of IT

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per change; configuration drift is compared to baseline monthly and the full change population is tested quarterly, with a complete re-walk of the traceability matrix annually

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly configuration-control workpaper (change extract, sample, approval evidence, baseline diff, regression results, exception list) filed in the compliance evidence repository under REG-014-C03

checklist.step: Write the configuration requirements straight from the rule text
actions: Open the current text of FINRA Rules 1240(b), 2210(d)(1) and 2211 on the FINRA Rulebook and copy the operative sentence of each obligation into a requirement row.
Translate each sentence into a testable system rule - for example 'a communication template cannot reach status Active without a recorded principal approval id and approval date'.

Record for each requirement the system, the object, the field and the enforcement type (hard block, warning, or report only), and mark any report-only control as a risk acceptance requiring compliance sign-off.
Have the Compliance Analyst confirm each translation against the rule before build starts.
Baseline the requirement set with a version number and attach the rule text so a future reader can re-derive it.
checklist.done: every in-scope rule sentence has a versioned, testable requirement with system, object, field and enforcement type, confirmed by Compliance.

checklist.step: Hold every regulatory deadline as a parameter, never as hard-coded logic
actions: Create a deadline parameter table holding rule cite, window value, unit (calendar days or business days), calendar id and effective-from date.
Load the values: 30 calendar days for the Rule 4530 clocks, 10 business days for Rule 2210(c) filings, December 31 for Firm Element completion.
Point every due-date computation at the parameter table so a rule change is a data change with an effective date, not a code release.
Attach the exchange holiday calendar to the business-day parameters and confirm it is maintained annually by the Operations Manager.
Restrict write access on the parameter table to a change-controlled role and alert Compliance on any edit.
checklist.done: all deadline windows are parameterised with rule cite, unit, calendar and effective date, and edits are access-restricted and alerted.

checklist.step: Configure the principal-approval gate on communications
actions: Add mandatory fields to the template object: principal approval id, approver name, approval date, and communication category under Rule 2210(a).
Block the status transition to Active where any of those fields is empty, and prevent the approver from being the same user as the author.
Add the AREF filing fields (submission number, first-use date) and warn on activation of a retail communication category with no submission number after 10 business days from first use.
Write a rejection message that names the missing field so the user can self-correct rather than raising a ticket.
Demonstrate the block to the Marketing Compliance Analyst in a non-production environment before release.
checklist.done: no communication template can go Active without a principal approval by a different user, demonstrated in a non-production environment.

checklist.step: Flag the FINRA-required notices as non-suppressible
actions: In the correspondence configuration set the Regulatory Required flag on the SIPC account-opening and annual notice, transaction confirms, contract-change notices and complaint acknowledgements.
Change the suppression engine so do-not-mail, householding and marketing preference rules are evaluated only for notices without that flag.
Leave the litigation-hold suppression path in place but require a named approver and reason code written to the notice log row.
Run a suppression simulation over one month of history and confirm zero regulatory-required notices would have been suppressed.
checklist.done: a one-month simulation shows no regulatory-required notice can be suppressed by any preference rule.

checklist.step: Configure Firm Element assignment and the December 31 enforcement
actions: Build the covered-person rule in the learning management system: any person with an active registration and a variable-product selling role is assigned the Firm Element curriculum on hire, on registration and at each annual cycle open.
Feed the registration status daily from the licensing record so a newly registered person is assigned within one business day.
Set the curriculum due date to December 31 of the assignment year and configure escalation notices at 60, 30 and 10 days out to the learner and their supervising principal.
Configure the January 1 status flip to Non-Compliant and expose that status to the supervision dashboard so restrictions can be applied.
Test with a synthetic learner record through hire, assignment, escalation and non-completion.
checklist.done: a synthetic learner proves automatic assignment, the December 31 due date, the three escalations and the January 1 non-compliant flip.

checklist.step: Configure the complaint case type that feeds the Rule 4513 file
actions: Create the Written Customer Complaint case type with mandatory fields for OSJ, associated person, product, FINRA problem and product codes, receipt date and action taken.
Block case closure where action taken is blank, since Rule 4513 requires the action recorded alongside the complaint.
Configure the daily feed from the case tool into the OSJ complaint file in the evidence repository with a 4-year retention label.
Configure the quarterly extract that supports the Rule 4530(d) statistical reporting so the same source drives both the file and the filing.
checklist.done: the complaint case type enforces its mandatory fields, cannot close without action taken, and feeds both the OSJ file and the quarterly extract.

checklist.step: Route every FINRA-touching change through change control with a compliance approval
actions: Add a Regulatory Control Affected field to the change form with a picklist of the FINRA controls and make it mandatory for changes on the in-scope systems.
Configure the approval workflow so any change with a FINRA control selected requires the Head of Compliance as a mandatory approver before the implementation task opens.
Require the change record to carry the requirement id, the regression test evidence and a back-out plan.
Block the standard-change fast path for any change touching a FINRA control, so it cannot be pre-approved as routine.
checklist.done: no change touching a FINRA control can reach implementation without a compliance approval, requirement id, test evidence and back-out plan.

checklist.step: Build and maintain the regression pack for the FINRA controls
actions: Write one automated test per requirement: due-date computation for each parameter, template activation blocked without approval, suppression blocked on regulatory notices, CE assignment on registration, complaint closure blocked without action taken.
Include boundary cases - a 30-calendar-day clock crossing a month end and a leap day, a 10-business-day clock crossing a market holiday, and a December 31 falling on a weekend.
Attach each test to its requirement id so a failed test names the rule it breaks.
Run the pack on every release to the in-scope systems and block the pipeline on any failure rather than warning.
checklist.done: every requirement has a linked automated test including date boundary cases, and the pipeline blocks on failure.

checklist.step: Prove the configuration behaves in a production-like environment before release
actions: Refresh the pre-production environment with masked production data so the tests run against realistic contract and registration volumes.
Execute the regression pack plus the change-specific scenarios and record pass/fail per requirement id.
Have the Compliance Analyst witness the tests for the requirements marked hard block and sign the results.
Attach the signed results to the change record; a change with an unsigned hard-block test does not release.
checklist.done: the regression pack has passed in a production-like environment with the hard-block results witnessed and signed by Compliance.

checklist.step: Release under a controlled window with a verified back-out
actions: Schedule the release inside the approved window and outside the statement and confirm generation cycles so no notice is generated mid-deployment.
Export the pre-change configuration for every touched object and store it against the change record as the back-out baseline.
Deploy through the pipeline only - no direct edits in production - and record the pipeline run id on the change.
Verify the deployed values against the approved requirement immediately after release and, on any difference, execute the back-out rather than fixing forward.
checklist.done: the release ran through the pipeline inside the window, with a stored pre-change export and a verified post-release value check.

checklist.step: Run the post-implementation verification with live data
actions: On the first business day after release, take 10 live trigger events and confirm the due dates computed match the parameter values and calendars.
Attempt to activate a test communication template with no approval id and confirm the block fires in production.
Attempt to suppress a regulatory-required notice on a test contract and confirm it is not suppressed.
Record the results on the change record and close the change only when all checks pass.
checklist.done: post-implementation checks on live data confirm every hard block fires in production, and the change is closed on the evidence.

checklist.step: Detect configuration drift against the approved baseline
actions: Schedule a monthly export of every in-scope parameter, flag and workflow rule from the three systems.
Diff the export against the approved baseline held in the source repository and list every difference with the object, old value, new value and last-modified user.
For each difference, find the change record; a difference with no change record is a drift exception raised the same day.
Update the baseline only after the Head of Compliance approves the difference, never silently on the next export.
checklist.done: the monthly diff is produced, each difference is matched to a change record, and unmatched differences are raised as drift exceptions.

checklist.step: Control emergency changes without losing the compliance approval
actions: Permit an emergency change to a FINRA control only with verbal authorisation from the Head of Compliance recorded on the change within one hour.
Require the full requirement, test evidence and retrospective approval to be attached within 3 business days of the emergency change.
Compute the exposure window - the period the control was weakened - and record which notices or templates passed through it.
Report every emergency change on a FINRA control to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
checklist.done: each emergency change carries a same-hour compliance authorisation, retrospective evidence within 3 business days and a stated exposure window.

checklist.step: Manage access so the controls cannot be edited outside change control
actions: Define the configuration-administrator entitlements on the three in-scope systems and remove them from any standing user role.
Grant them only through a time-boxed elevation tied to an approved change record, expiring automatically at the end of the window.
Recertify the entitlement holders quarterly with the IT Service Delivery Manager and the Head of Compliance as joint approvers.
Alert Compliance on any use of the entitlement with no open change record.
checklist.done: configuration-administrator access is time-boxed to approved changes, quarterly recertified and alerted on use without a change record.

checklist.step: Keep the traceability matrix current with the rulebook
actions: Review new FINRA Regulatory Notices weekly and mark any that touch Rules 1240, 2210, 2211, 4513 or 4530.
For each marked notice, walk the traceability matrix and identify every requirement, parameter and test that must change, with the notice's effective date.
Raise the change requests so configuration is live before the effective date, not on it.
Version the matrix, record the driving notice number, and report unmapped rule changes to the Head of Compliance monthly.
checklist.done: the matrix carries a version and the driving FINRA notice number, with change requests raised ahead of each effective date.

testing.step: Build the population of FINRA-affecting changes and live parameters
actions: Extract every change record in the period with a target of the policy administration, learning management or case management systems, regardless of whether the Regulatory Control Affected flag was set.
Extract the live values of every in-scope parameter, non-suppressible flag, approval gate and CE assignment rule as at the test date.
Reconcile the change extract to the deployment pipeline run history so a release without a change record is visible.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date, record count and reconciling items.
testing.done: the change population reconciles to pipeline runs and a dated live-configuration export exists, both signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the live configuration to the approved baseline
actions: Diff the live configuration export against the approved baseline held in the source repository, object by object.
For each difference, locate the approving change record and confirm the Head of Compliance approval pre-dates the deployment.
List every difference with no change record as an automatic exception, recording the last-modified user and timestamp.
Confirm the 30-calendar-day and 10-business-day windows and the December 31 date in the live export match the rule text, not just the baseline.
testing.done: every live-versus-baseline difference is matched to an approved change or listed as an exception, and the deadline values match the rule text.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of changes
actions: Take 100% of emergency changes and 100% of changes touching a deadline parameter.
Take 100% of changes where the Regulatory Control Affected flag was not set but the target object appears in the traceability matrix.
Take 20 further changes at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population, minimum 35 items overall.
Record the seed, strata, population sizes and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all emergency and parameter changes plus mis-flagged changes, and is reproducible from the recorded seed.

testing.step: Verify approval, evidence and segregation on each sampled change
actions: For each sampled change, confirm the requirement id, the Head of Compliance approval and the signed regression results are attached and dated before the deployment timestamp.
Confirm the implementer is a different person from the approver and from the requester.
Confirm a back-out plan and a pre-change configuration export exist.
Treat approval dated after deployment as an exception equal in severity to no approval at all.
testing.done: each sampled change shows pre-dated compliance approval, signed test evidence, a back-out plan and separation of requester, approver and implementer.

testing.step: Re-perform the deadline computation against the rule text
actions: Take 15 live trigger events across the notice types and recompute the due date by hand from the trigger date, the rule window and the exchange holiday calendar.
Include boundary cases: a 30-calendar-day clock crossing a month end, a 10-business-day clock crossing a market holiday, and a December 31 falling at a weekend.
Compare each hand computation to the system-held due date and flag any difference as a configuration exception.
Attach the calculation sheet including the holiday calendar used to the workpaper.
testing.done: 15 hand-recomputed due dates including boundary cases agree with the system, or the differences are logged as configuration exceptions.

testing.step: Attempt the blocked actions in a controlled environment
actions: Using a test record, attempt to activate a communication template with no principal approval id and record the system response.
Attempt to activate a template where the approver equals the author and record the response.
Attempt to apply a do-not-mail suppression to a regulatory-required notice and record the response.
Attempt to close a written complaint case with the action-taken field blank and record the response.
Capture a screenshot of each attempt and its rejection message into the workpaper; a warning where a hard block was specified is an exception.
testing.done: every specified hard block is proven to fire on a live attempt, with screenshots and rejection messages captured.

testing.step: Test the Firm Element assignment rule against the registration record
actions: Take the population of persons with an active registration and a variable-product selling role from the licensing record as at three dates spread across the year.
Join to the learning management system assignment record and list anyone active but unassigned, and anyone assigned with a due date other than December 31.
For 10 people registered mid-year, check the assignment appeared within one business day of the registration date.
Confirm the January 1 non-compliant flip actually applied to those outstanding at year end.
testing.done: every actively registered covered person is assigned with a December 31 due date, mid-year assignments landed within one business day, and the January 1 flip applied.

testing.step: Test privileged access to the configuration
actions: Extract every holder of a configuration-administrator entitlement on the in-scope systems during the period, including time-boxed grants.
Match each grant to an approved change record covering the grant window and list unmatched grants as exceptions.
Confirm the quarterly recertification was completed by both the IT Service Delivery Manager and the Head of Compliance, with dated evidence.
Review the system audit log for configuration edits made outside a grant window.
testing.done: every privileged grant maps to an approved change window, recertifications are dated and signed, and no out-of-window edits are unexplained.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the change id or object name, the control affected, the FINRA rule at risk and the exposure window in days.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: control not flagged, approval obtained late, test evidence missing, emergency path abused, drift with no change record, access outside change control.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and determine with the Head of Compliance whether the exposure window requires a look-back over the notices or templates processed during it.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with an exposure window, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date, a look-back decision and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception count against the zero-tolerance threshold for unapproved FINRA-control changes and baseline drift.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who raised, built, approved or deployed none of the sampled changes, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the result, every emergency change and every drift exception to the Compliance Committee and the technology risk forum, and file the workpaper under REG-014-C03.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the exception count, a stated conclusion and dated reporting to both committees is filed in the evidence repository.
