Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Needs analysis completed by 31 March, written plan approved by 30 April, delivery open by 30 June, all covered persons complete by 31 December; the separate Regulatory Element under Rule 1240(a) also completes in FinPro by 31 December

Deadline reminders configured.value: Learning system escalations to learner and supervising principal at 60, 30 and 10 days before 31 December, plus milestone alerts to the Compliance Manager at the March, April and June plan dates

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Needs analysis working papers, the approved written plan, course content versions, attendance and completion records and assessment scores retained 6 years, and made available at each office of supervisory jurisdiction on request

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every covered person outstanding at 31 December is logged with their CRD number, supervising principal, the restriction applied on 1 January and the date the training was finally completed

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off the annual plan, and signs off each non-completion case including the registered-activity restriction and its lifting

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All persons holding an active registration and a variable-product selling or supervisory role at any point in the training year, taken from the licensing record, joined to their learning system assignment and completion status

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of covered persons complete the Firm Element by 31 December; a documented needs analysis and an approved written plan must exist before delivery opened; any person selling variable products after 1 January while outstanding is a reportable supervisory breach, not a training exception

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the completion population is tested in January against the prior year, with an interim coverage test each quarter to catch mid-year registrations that were never assigned

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Compliance and Learning and must not have authored the plan or administered any sampled completion

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual Firm Element test workpaper (roster reconciliation, assignment coverage, completion evidence, content-to-needs traceability, exception list) filed in the compliance evidence repository under REG-014-C04

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Needs analysis, approved written training plan, course outlines with the variable-product modules identified, and a completion report by CRD number - producible for a FINRA cycle exam Rule 1240 request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance owns the examiner request; Regulatory Counsel clears any response disclosing persons who transacted while non-compliant

checklist.step: Define the covered-person population from the registration record
actions: Extract every person with an active securities registration and an active state insurance appointment for variable products, with CRD number, registration categories, appointment states and supervising principal.
Include registered supervisors and principals, since Firm Element covers persons who supervise covered activity as well as those who sell it.
Exclude persons whose only registration lapsed before the training year opened and record the exclusion reason against each name.
Agree the definition in writing with the Head of Compliance and freeze the roster as the covered-person baseline for the year.
Set the roster to refresh daily so new registrations join the population automatically.
checklist.done: a frozen, written covered-person definition and a daily-refreshing roster keyed on CRD number exist and are agreed by the Head of Compliance.

checklist.step: Assemble the needs-analysis evidence base
actions: Pull the prior year's customer complaints by product and problem code from the complaints queue, isolating variable annuity and variable life matters.

Pull suitability review outcomes, exchange and replacement rates, surrender activity within the surrender charge period, and any pattern of unsuitable recommendations from the Annuity Suitability Analyst.
Pull supervisory findings: branch examination results, correspondence review flags, trade blotter exceptions and any FINRA or state examination deficiency letters.
Pull the FINRA Regulatory Notices issued in the year and the annual FINRA Regulatory Oversight Report priorities relevant to variable products.
Load all of it into one needs-analysis workbook with the source and date of each input.
checklist.done: one workbook holds complaint, suitability, supervisory and regulatory-development inputs, each with a named source and date.

checklist.step: Run and document the annual needs analysis
actions: Score each input for frequency and potential customer harm and rank the resulting training needs.
Segment the needs by audience: new registered persons, experienced variable annuity producers, supervising principals, and the internal wholesaling and service population.
Write the analysis conclusion in narrative form naming the specific products, services and strategies the firm offers and the risks each carries, as Rule 1240(b) requires.
Include the regulatory developments of the year with the FINRA notice numbers.
Date and sign the analysis and complete it by 31 March so the plan can be built against it.
checklist.done: a dated, signed needs analysis exists by 31 March, ranking needs by audience and naming the products and regulatory developments driving them.

checklist.step: Write the annual training plan against the analysis
actions: Write the plan with a row per training need showing the module that addresses it, the audience, the delivery channel, the duration, the assessment and the completion deadline.
Trace every module back to a numbered need from the analysis so nothing appears in the plan without a driver and no ranked need goes unaddressed.
State explicitly which modules cover variable annuities and variable insurance products under Rule 2211 and which cover the year's regulatory developments.
Submit the plan to the Head of Compliance and the designated supervisory principal for approval by 30 April.
Version the approved plan and publish it where supervising principals can read it.
checklist.done: an approved, versioned written plan exists by 30 April with every module traced to a numbered need and every ranked need addressed.

checklist.step: Build the course content to the plan
actions: Build each module to the plan row: learning objectives, scenario content drawn from the firm's own complaints and suitability findings, and a knowledge check.
Write the variable annuity module around the firm's actual contracts - living benefit riders, surrender charge schedules, sub-account line-up and the exchange and replacement rules.
Set the assessment pass mark at 80% with a maximum of three attempts, after which the learner is routed to instructor-led remediation.
Have the Annuity Suitability Analyst and Regulatory Counsel review the content for technical and legal accuracy before publication.
Version each module and record the plan row it satisfies in the module metadata.
checklist.done: every plan row has a published, reviewed module with objectives, firm-specific scenarios, an 80% assessment and the plan row recorded in its metadata.

checklist.step: Assign the curriculum and open delivery
actions: Assign the curriculum by audience segment from the daily-refreshing covered-person roster, with a 31 December due date.
Open delivery by 30 June and notify each learner and their supervising principal with the deadline and the consequence of non-completion.
Configure the auto-assignment rule so anyone newly registered mid-year is assigned within one business day and given at least 60 days or the remainder of the year, whichever is shorter.
Confirm accessibility - the modules run on the field's tablets and are captioned - so no one has a delivery excuse.
checklist.done: delivery is open by 30 June, every covered person is assigned with a 31 December due date, and mid-year registrants auto-assign within one business day.

checklist.step: Deliver the instructor-led sessions for supervising principals
actions: Schedule the principal sessions covering supervisory review of variable annuity recommendations, correspondence review and complaint handling under Rule 4513.
Take attendance from the meeting join report rather than a show-of-hands and load it into the learning record within two business days.
Run the case exercises using redacted firm complaints so principals practise on real fact patterns.
Record the session and publish it for anyone who could not attend, with the same assessment applied.
checklist.done: each principal session has a system-derived attendance record loaded to the learning record within two business days, and a recorded catch-up option.

checklist.step: Track completion weekly and escalate the outstanding
actions: Publish a weekly completion dashboard from the learning system split by supervising principal, region and audience segment.
Send the outstanding list to each supervising principal weekly from 1 October, naming individuals and days remaining.
Fire the automated escalations at 60, 30 and 10 days before 31 December to the learner and copy the principal.
Report completion percentage to the Head of Compliance monthly and weekly through December.
checklist.done: the weekly dashboard runs, principals receive named outstanding lists from 1 October and the three deadline escalations have fired.

checklist.step: Manage the separate annual Regulatory Element in parallel
actions: Pull each registered person's Regulatory Element status from FINRA's FinPro and CRD and record the annual 31 December requirement per registration category.
Notify anyone outstanding at 60 and 30 days out, since failure to complete the Regulatory Element makes the registration inactive and stops them transacting.
Reconcile FinPro status to the internal roster monthly so a registration that has gone CE Inactive is caught within a month, not at year end.
Report any CE Inactive registration to the supervising principal and the Head of Compliance the same day.
checklist.done: Regulatory Element status is reconciled to the roster monthly and every CE Inactive registration is escalated the same day it is found.

checklist.step: Remediate learners who fail the assessment
actions: Pull the list of learners who exhausted three attempts and route them to an instructor-led remediation session.
Cover the specific questions failed rather than repeating the whole module, and re-assess at the end of the session.
Record the remediation attendance and the final score in the learning record and notify the supervising principal.
Where a learner fails after remediation, refer to the Head of Compliance for a decision on restricting their variable-product activity.
checklist.done: every learner who exhausted their attempts has a recorded remediation session, a final score and, where still failing, a referral decision.

checklist.step: Apply and record the 1 January restriction on the outstanding
actions: On 1 January, take the list of covered persons still outstanding and open a case per person with CRD number and supervising principal.
Instruct the Distribution Operations Manager to block new variable-product business submission for each named person until completion.
Notify the person and their principal in writing that they may not engage in the covered activity until the Firm Element is complete.
Lift the restriction only on evidence of completion, recording the completion date and the lift date on the case.
checklist.done: every person outstanding at 1 January has a case, a submission block, a written notification and a dated lift on completion.

checklist.step: Handle new hires, transfers and leavers within the cycle
actions: Feed hire, role change, leave of absence and termination events daily from the HR system to the learning system and the licensing record.
On a role change into a variable-product selling or supervisory role, trigger the covered-person assignment the same day.
For a person on extended leave crossing 31 December, record the deferral decision and the revised deadline approved by the Head of Compliance.
On termination, close the assignment and retain the partial completion record rather than deleting it.
checklist.done: hire, transfer, leave and termination events flow daily, role changes trigger same-day assignment and deferrals carry a written approval.

checklist.step: Reconcile the learning record to the registration record
actions: Join the licensing record to the learning system assignment on CRD number monthly and list anyone registered with no assignment, and anyone assigned with no active registration.
Investigate every break within 5 business days and record the cause - late registration feed, name mismatch, contractor record outside HR.
Publish the break count and ageing on the completion dashboard so an unassigned population cannot hide behind a high completion percentage.
Escalate any break older than 15 business days to the Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: the monthly CRD-level reconciliation runs with every break investigated inside 5 business days and ageing published on the dashboard.

checklist.step: File the annual evidence pack
actions: Assemble the pack: needs analysis with its inputs, the approved written plan with version history, module content versions and reviewer sign-offs, assignment and completion extracts by CRD number, assessment scores, escalation logs and restriction cases.
File it under REG-014-C04 with the training year in the folder name and apply a 6-year retention label.
Confirm the pack is retrievable by CRD number and by module, since examiners ask about named individuals.
Make the pack available to each office of supervisory jurisdiction on request.
checklist.done: the annual pack is filed, 6-year retention labelled and retrievable by CRD number and module.

checklist.step: Close the cycle and feed next year's analysis
actions: Write a close report covering completion rate, exception count, assessment failure hot spots and the modules with the worst scores.
Carry the weak topics forward as named inputs into the next needs analysis rather than starting the analysis from scratch.
Present the close report to the Compliance Committee in January with the restriction cases still open.
Record the committee's directions as inputs to the next plan.
checklist.done: a January close report exists with completion rate, failure hot spots, open restrictions and committee directions carried into the next needs analysis.

testing.step: Build the covered-person population independently
actions: Extract from the licensing record every person with an active securities registration and variable-product appointment at any point in the training year, with start and end dates.
Add supervising principals and internal wholesalers with covered activity so the population is not limited to producers.
Reconcile the extract to the payroll and contractor registers to catch anyone paid to sell who is missing from the licensing feed.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date, the headcount and the reconciling items.
testing.done: an independently built covered-person population reconciles to payroll and contractor registers and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the audit population to the firm's roster and assignments
actions: Join the audit population to the firm's covered-person roster on CRD number and list anyone the firm omitted.
Join to the learning system assignment record and list anyone in the population with no assignment at all.
Check the assignment due date on every row equals 31 December of the training year.
List every unmatched or wrongly dated row as an automatic exception with the person's CRD number and supervising principal.
testing.done: the population, roster and assignment records reconcile three ways, with unmatched or wrongly dated rows listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of learners and modules
actions: Take 100% of persons registered mid-year and 100% of persons who completed in the last 10 days of December, since both are where the process strains.
Take 100% of persons subject to a 1 January restriction in the prior cycle.
Take 25 further learners at random with a recorded seed, minimum 40 people overall, plus every module in the plan.
Record the seed, strata, population sizes and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers mid-year registrants, late completers and prior restrictions and is reproducible from the recorded seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the needs analysis linkage
actions: Independently pull the year's variable-product complaints, suitability exceptions and examination findings and rank the top themes without reading the firm's analysis.
Compare your top themes to the ranked needs in the firm's analysis and question any theme the firm omitted.
Trace each module in the plan back to a numbered need and each ranked need forward to a module; list needs with no module as a coverage gap.
Confirm the analysis names the firm's actual products, services and strategies rather than generic industry topics, as Rule 1240(b) requires.
testing.done: an independent theme ranking is compared to the firm's, and every need traces to a module and every module to a need or is logged as a gap.

testing.step: Verify the plan approval predates delivery
actions: Open the approved plan version and read the approval signatures and dates of the Head of Compliance and the designated supervisory principal.
Compare the approval date to the delivery-open date recorded in the learning system; delivery opened before approval is an exception.
Confirm the needs analysis is dated before the plan and both fall inside the stated 31 March and 30 April milestones.
Check the version history for edits made after approval and confirm each carries a re-approval.
testing.done: the analysis, the plan approval and the delivery-open date are in the correct order and inside the milestone dates, with post-approval edits re-approved.

testing.step: Trace sampled completions to underlying evidence
actions: For each sampled learner, open the transcript and confirm module completion timestamps, assessment score and the number of attempts.
For instructor-led modules, trace the completion to the meeting attendance report rather than accepting a manually keyed completion.
Check for implausible completions - a 60-minute module completed in under 10 minutes, or several modules completed in the same minute - and list them for investigation.
Confirm any manually recorded completion carries a named recorder and a documented reason.
testing.done: each sampled completion traces to a timestamped transcript and, for instructor-led modules, to an attendance report, with implausible completions listed.

testing.step: Recompute completion rates and the deadline position
actions: Recompute the completion percentage from the audit population, not the firm's roster, since a narrow roster inflates the rate.
Count anyone whose completion timestamp falls after 31 December as outstanding at the deadline regardless of a later completion.
For mid-year registrants, recompute whether they received the required window from their registration date to the deadline.
Show both the firm's stated rate and the recomputed rate side by side in the workpaper with the difference explained.
testing.done: the recomputed completion rate is stated alongside the firm's rate with the difference explained, and post-deadline completions are counted as outstanding.

testing.step: Test that non-completion actually stopped the activity
actions: Take everyone outstanding at 1 January and extract every variable-product application, exchange and additional-purchase transaction they wrote between 1 January and their completion date.
Any transaction in that window is a supervisory breach, not a training exception - record the contract numbers and premium involved.
Confirm a restriction case, a written notification and a submission block existed for each person, with dates.
Confirm the block was lifted only after evidenced completion.
testing.done: no outstanding person transacted after 1 January, or every such transaction is recorded as a supervisory breach with contract numbers and premium.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the CRD number, supervising principal, the failure type and the days beyond deadline.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: person missing from the roster, assignment not triggered, escalation not sent, restriction not applied, completion recorded without evidence, content gap against the needs analysis.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and decide with Regulatory Counsel whether any breach requires reporting under Rule 4530.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle's interim quarterly coverage test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with CRD number and days late, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a Rule 4530 reporting decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare the recomputed completion rate to the 100% threshold and state the count of persons outstanding at 31 December.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the needs-analysis coverage, the approval sequence and the completion evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Compliance and Learning and administered no sampled completion, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and the Audit Committee in the January cycle and file the signed workpaper under REG-014-C04.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating the recomputed completion rate, outstanding count, conclusion and committee reporting dates is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the FINRA complaint lifecycle for variable products - capture, coding, the quarterly Rule 4530(d) statistical filing, the Rule 4530(f) document copies and root-cause remediation; escalates trends to the Head of Compliance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - FINRA Rule 4530(d) (quarterly statistical and summary information on customer complaints), Rule 4530(f) (copies of criminal indictments or informations, civil complaints and arbitration claims within 30 calendar days), Rule 4513 (complaint file at each office of supervisory jurisdiction) and Rule 2210(d)(8), re-read on the FINRA Rulebook each quarter before the filing is prepared

In-scope processes.value: Continuous complaint intake across all advertised channels, classification and FINRA problem/product coding, investigation and response, quarterly statistical reporting, 4530(f) document filing, trend analysis and root-cause remediation across variable annuity and variable life business

In-scope systems.value: Complaint case record of source, coding, associated person, investigation and outcome; feeds the OSJ complaint files, the quarterly 4530(d) extract and the trend dashboard

Compliance procedure documented.value: Complaint Handling and FINRA Reporting Procedure - what counts as a written customer complaint, day-zero for each clock, problem and product code selection rules, investigation standard, response timeframes, quarterly filing preparation and the root-cause remediation route

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and reviewed with Regulatory Counsel each year and after any FINRA Regulatory Notice changing the 4530 codes or filing mechanics

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Rule 4530(d) statistical and summary complaint information filed by the 15th day of the month following each calendar quarter end (15 January, 15 April, 15 July, 15 October); Rule 4530(f) copies within 30 calendar days of receipt; internal acknowledgement of a complaint within 5 business days and substantive response within 30 calendar days

Deadline reminders configured.value: Case timers fire on acknowledgement day 3 and day 5 and on response day 20 and day 27; quarterly filing milestones alert the owner on the 1st, 8th and 12th of January, April, July and October

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Written complaints and the action taken retained 4 years per FINRA Rule 4513 and held at the relevant office of supervisory jurisdiction; 4530 submissions and acknowledgements retained 6 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Miscoded complaints, complaints not routed to the complaints function, late or omitted 4530(d) rows, late 4530(f) copies and overdue responses are each logged with the case number, days late, root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late or amended 4530 filing and every systemic root-cause remediation plan arising from complaint trends

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of reportable complaints appear in the quarterly filing with correct problem and product codes; 100% of 4530(f) documents filed within 30 calendar days; complaint acknowledgement within 5 business days at 98% or better; any complaint routed but never logged is a fail regardless of outcome

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous with a quarterly filing; testing runs quarterly on the filed population immediately after each 15th-day submission, with a monthly channel-sweep for unlogged complaints

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly complaint-reporting test workpaper (channel sweep, case extract, coding re-performance, filing reconciliation, ageing calculation, exception list) filed in the compliance evidence repository under REG-014-C05

checklist.step: Sweep every advertised channel into the complaint queue daily
actions: Work the shared complaints mailbox, the web form queue, the postal intake scan batch and the contact-centre complaint dispositions each morning and open a case for each contact.
Pull the prior day's escalations from the Contact Center Supervisor and from the Broker Relationship Manager for broker-sourced complaints so field-received letters are captured centrally.
Enter receipt date as the date the firm first received the contact - the postmark or email timestamp - not the date the case was opened.
Set case type to Written Customer Complaint for anything in writing, since that is what drives Rule 4513 and the 4530(d) filing.
Leave the intake queue at zero each day and record any item that could not be opened with the reason.
checklist.done: every advertised channel is emptied daily into cases carrying the true receipt date, and the intake queue closes at zero.

checklist.step: Classify each complaint and apply the FINRA problem and product codes
actions: Read the complaint and decide reportable versus non-reportable against the Rule 4530(d) criteria, recording the reasoning in the case note.
Select the FINRA product code for the contract involved - variable annuity, variable life, mutual fund - from the code list published in the 4530 filing application.

Select the problem code that matches the customer's actual grievance (for example unsuitable recommendation, misrepresentation, unauthorised transaction, fees and charges, service delay) rather than the most convenient code.
Record the associated person named, their CRD number, the branch and the office of supervisory jurisdiction.
Have a second analyst peer-review the coding on any complaint alleging sales practice misconduct before the case advances.
checklist.done: each complaint carries a reportability decision with reasoning, product and problem codes, the named associated person with CRD number and a peer review on sales-practice allegations.

checklist.step: Acknowledge the customer inside 5 business days
actions: Send the acknowledgement letter or email within 5 business days of receipt, naming the case reference, the handler and the expected response date.
Include the firm's complaint contact details and the statement that the customer may also contact FINRA, matching the wording on the published disclosure block.
Record the acknowledgement send date on the case from the correspondence history, not by hand.
Escalate to the Complaints Manager on day 3 for any case with no acknowledgement drafted.
checklist.done: every case shows a system-recorded acknowledgement inside 5 business days, or an escalation raised on day 3.

checklist.step: Investigate the complaint against the transaction and suitability record
actions: Pull the contract record: application, suitability form, illustration used, replacement or exchange documentation, rider elections, transaction history and surrender charge schedule.
Pull the associated person's correspondence with the customer from the surveillance archive and read what was actually said.
Test the recommendation against the suitability record at the time of sale - age, time horizon, liquidity needs, existing holdings, source of funds.
Interview the associated person and the supervising principal where sales practice is alleged, and record the interview notes on the case.
State a written finding: substantiated, partly substantiated, or not substantiated, with the evidence behind it.
checklist.done: each investigated case carries the contract and suitability evidence, correspondence review, interview notes where relevant and a written substantiation finding.

checklist.step: Respond to the customer within 30 calendar days
actions: Draft a substantive response addressing each allegation, stating the finding and any redress offered, and have Regulatory Counsel review anything alleging misrepresentation or unauthorised trading.
Send within 30 calendar days of receipt; where more time is genuinely needed, send a holding letter that gives a date and record the reason on the case.
Record redress - refund, contract reinstatement, fee waiver, commission chargeback - with the amount and the approval.
Enter action taken on the case, since Rule 4513 requires the action recorded alongside the complaint, and the case cannot close without it.
checklist.done: a substantive response is sent within 30 calendar days with the finding, any redress amount and the action-taken field completed.

checklist.step: Maintain the Rule 4513 complaint file at each office of supervisory jurisdiction
actions: Feed each closed written complaint and its action taken into the file for the OSJ that supervises the associated person, daily.
Apply a 4-year retention label and confirm the record is retrievable by OSJ, associated person, complainant and receipt date.
Reconcile each OSJ file to the case extract monthly and open a gap item for anything present in one and missing from the other.
Confirm each OSJ can produce its file on an examiner's request without a central request queue.
checklist.done: every OSJ file is fed daily, retention-labelled for 4 years, monthly reconciled to the case extract and producible locally.

checklist.step: File the quarterly Rule 4530(d) statistical and summary information
actions: On the first business day after quarter end, extract every reportable complaint received in the quarter with its product code, problem code, associated person CRD number and receipt date.
Reconcile the extract count to the case management total and to the prior quarter's carry-forward before entering anything.
Enter the statistical and summary information in the FINRA Gateway Rule 4530 application, or upload the file in the prescribed format, and validate every row before submission.
Submit by the 15th day of the month following quarter end - 15 January, 15 April, 15 July, 15 October - and record the submission id and timestamp.
Where a prior quarter must be corrected, file an amendment and record the reason and the Head of Compliance approval on the issue.
checklist.done: the quarterly filing is submitted by the 15th with a recorded submission id and a reconciliation from the case extract to the submitted rows.

checklist.step: File Rule 4530(f) document copies within 30 calendar days
actions: Register every criminal indictment or information, civil complaint and arbitration claim naming the firm or an associated person on the day it is received, with the true receipt date.
Assess it against Rule 4530(f) and record the assessment even where the conclusion is that no filing is required.
Upload the copy through the FINRA Gateway Rule 4530 application within 30 calendar days of receipt, targeting day 20 to leave buffer.
Record the submission id on the matter and notify the Producer Compliance Manager so any Form U4 disclosure amendment is assessed in parallel.
Report any document approaching day 25 without submission to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every registered document has a written 4530(f) assessment and, where required, a submission id inside 30 calendar days of receipt.

checklist.step: Run the monthly complaint trend analysis
actions: Publish complaint volume and rate per 1,000 contracts by product, problem code, associated person, branch and OSJ, with a rolling 13-month trend.
Set thresholds that trigger review: any associated person with 3 or more complaints in 12 months, any problem code up more than 25% quarter on quarter, any branch above twice the firm average.
Overlay surrender and exchange activity so a sales-practice pattern shows up even where the customer never complained.
Circulate the dashboard to the Head of Compliance, the supervising principals and the Distribution Operations Manager monthly.
checklist.done: the monthly dashboard publishes rates and trends against the stated thresholds and is circulated to compliance, supervision and distribution.

checklist.step: Escalate individual associated persons who breach the threshold
actions: Open a heightened supervision review on any associated person crossing the complaint threshold, listing every complaint, its outcome and the redress paid.
Pull their full book for the period and re-review a sample of variable annuity recommendations against the suitability record.
Agree the action with the supervising principal: additional training, pre-approval of recommendations, restricted product authority, or referral for disciplinary action.
Record the plan, the review dates and the exit criteria on the case, and assess whether the outcome is reportable under Rule 4530(a).
checklist.done: each threshold breach has a documented heightened supervision plan with a book re-review, agreed action, review dates and a 4530(a) reportability assessment.

checklist.step: Drive root-cause remediation into the business
actions: Group the quarter's complaints by root cause - illustration wording, surrender charge disclosure, service turnaround, statement clarity, replacement process - rather than by symptom.
For each cause above the materiality threshold, raise a remediation issue naming the owning function, the fix and the target date.
Feed content and form fixes to the Marketing Compliance Analyst and process fixes to the owning operations lead.
Track closure and re-measure the complaint rate for that cause the following quarter to prove the fix worked.
checklist.done: each material root cause has an owned remediation issue and a following-quarter re-measurement of the complaint rate for that cause.

checklist.step: Feed complaint themes into training and supervision
actions: Give the top complaint themes and redacted case studies to the Firm Element needs analysis as a named input.
Update the supervisory review checklists so principals check the specific behaviour the complaints exposed.
Brief the field on the quarter's themes through the distribution communication channel with the corrective expectation stated plainly.
Record the handover date and the receiving owner so the linkage is evidenced.
checklist.done: the quarter's themes are handed to the needs analysis and the supervisory checklists with a dated handover record.

checklist.step: Reconcile complaint sources so nothing bypasses the queue
actions: Load the contact-centre disposition extract, the shared mailbox log, the web form submissions, the postal scan index and the regulator and Better Business Bureau referral log each month.
Search free-text service notes for complaint language - dissatisfied, misled, complaint, attorney, arbitration - and list contacts with no matching complaint case.
Give the unmatched list to the Complaints Manager for same-week assessment and case opening where warranted.
Publish the leakage count monthly so the number is visible rather than assumed to be zero.
checklist.done: the monthly leakage sweep produces an unmatched list that is assessed within the week and a published leakage count.

checklist.step: Report to the Compliance Committee each quarter
actions: Present complaint volumes, rates, top problem codes, heightened supervision cases and redress paid for the quarter.
Report the 4530(d) filing date and submission id, any amendment filed, and every 4530(f) document filed with its day count.
Escalate any systemic issue that may require a Rule 4530(a) report or a self-report, with Regulatory Counsel's view attached.
Record the committee's directions and the owner and date for each.
checklist.done: a quarterly committee paper is tabled with filing evidence, trend data, escalations and recorded directions with owners and dates.

checklist.step: Archive the quarter's complaint evidence
actions: Archive the case extract behind the filing, the submitted 4530(d) file, its confirmation, every 4530(f) submission receipt and the trend dashboard snapshot.
File under REG-014-C05 by quarter and apply 4-year retention to complaint records and 6-year retention to the filings.
Confirm retrieval by case number, CRD number, contract number and quarter.
Test retrieval on 10 records and record the retrieval times.
checklist.done: the quarter's pack is archived with the correct retention labels and proven retrievable by case, CRD and contract number.

testing.step: Build the population of complaint contacts from source channels
actions: Extract independently from each channel of record: contact-centre dispositions, shared mailbox, web form, postal scan index, regulator and BBB referrals, and field-received correspondence.
Apply a complaint-language search across service notes and correspondence text to surface contacts that were never dispositioned as complaints.
Deduplicate on customer and contract and date so a single grievance across channels counts once.
Sign the population as complete, recording the extract date, channel counts and the deduplication rule applied.
testing.done: a deduplicated, channel-by-channel complaint population is built independently of the case system and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the case system and to the filed rows
actions: Match each population item to a complaint case and list unmatched contacts as leakage exceptions with the channel and date.
Match every reportable case to a row in the submitted quarterly 4530(d) file and list cases reportable but not filed.
Match every filed row back to a case and list filed rows with no case as data-integrity exceptions.
Reconcile the three counts in a single statement showing population, cases and filed rows with every difference explained.
testing.done: population, cases and filed rows reconcile in a single stated calculation with every difference explained or raised as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample weighted to risk
actions: Take 100% of complaints alleging unsuitable recommendation, misrepresentation or unauthorised transaction.
Take 100% of complaints against associated persons at or above the heightened supervision threshold, and 100% of 4530(f) documents.
Take 25 further complaints at random with a recorded seed from the remainder, minimum 40 cases overall.
Record the seed, strata, population sizes and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all sales-practice allegations, threshold producers and 4530(f) documents and is reproducible from the recorded seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the reportability decision and the coding
actions: Read each sampled complaint in full and reach an independent reportability decision against Rule 4530(d) before opening the firm's decision.
Select the product and problem codes independently from the code list in the FINRA 4530 application, then compare to the codes filed.
Treat a right reportability call with a wrong problem code as an exception - the statistical filing is only as good as the codes.
Record the independent decision, the firm's decision and the difference on each sampled row.
testing.done: each sampled complaint carries an independent reportability call and independent coding compared line by line to what was filed.

testing.step: Trace sampled cases to the OSJ complaint file
actions: For each sampled written complaint, retrieve the record from the file of the OSJ that supervises the named associated person.
Confirm the file holds the complaint itself and the action taken, as Rule 4513 requires, not merely a case summary.
Confirm the retention label is 4 years and the record is retrievable by associated person and receipt date.
List any complaint held centrally but absent from its OSJ file as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled complaint is retrieved from the correct OSJ file complete with the action taken and a 4-year retention label.

testing.step: Verify the quarterly filing was made on time and completely
actions: Open the submission record in the FINRA Gateway 4530 application and read the submission timestamp and id.
Compare the timestamp to the 15th day of the month following quarter end and record any days late.
Compare the submitted row count and code distribution to the reconciled case extract and investigate any difference greater than zero.
Where an amendment was filed, confirm the reason, the Head of Compliance approval and that the amendment corrected the whole error and not just the flagged row.
testing.done: the filing timestamp, row count and code distribution are verified against the case extract, with amendments confirmed as complete.

testing.step: Recompute the 30-day and 5-day clocks
actions: For each 4530(f) document, recompute due date as receipt date plus 30 calendar days from the matter register receipt date, not the case-open date, and compare to the submission date.
For each sampled complaint, recompute the acknowledgement due date as receipt plus 5 business days and the response due date as receipt plus 30 calendar days.
Where the receipt date on the case differs from the postmark or email timestamp, use the earlier date and record the shift as an exception in its own right.
State days late per item and attach the calculation to the workpaper.
testing.done: every clock is recomputed from the earliest evidenced receipt date with days late stated per item.

testing.step: Test that trends triggered the action they should have
actions: Recompute complaints per associated person over the rolling 12 months and identify everyone at or above the 3-complaint threshold.
Confirm a heightened supervision case exists for each, with a book re-review, an agreed action and review dates.
Recompute problem-code movement quarter on quarter and confirm every code above the 25% growth trigger has a remediation issue with an owner.
List any threshold breach with no case or no remediation issue as a control failure rather than a data observation.
testing.done: every recomputed threshold breach maps to a heightened supervision case or a remediation issue, or is logged as a control failure.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the case number, channel, associated person CRD, the rule breached and the days late or the miscode.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: contact never logged, receipt date shifted, reportability misjudged, code selected wrongly, filing incomplete, 4530(f) assessed late, OSJ file not fed.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and decide with Regulatory Counsel whether an amended filing or a self-report is required.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with the rule breached and days late, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and an amendment or self-report decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the coding accuracy rate, the filing completeness rate and the acknowledgement on-time rate against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the reconciliation, the re-performed coding and the clock recomputation.
Have the independent reviewer, who investigated, coded or filed none of the sampled complaints, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee at the next sitting with any amended filing decision and file the signed workpaper under REG-014-C05.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with coding accuracy, filing completeness, on-time rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Scope the audit from a documented risk assessment
actions: Rate each notice and communication type for inherent risk using volume, customer harm potential, regulatory attention and prior findings.
Read the prior year's audit findings, the compliance monitoring results, the complaint themes and any FINRA examination deficiency letters as scoping inputs.
Set the audit objective explicitly against FINRA Rules 2210(d)(1), 2210(c), 2211 and 1240(b) and name what is out of scope so the boundary is on the record.
Agree the scope with the Head of Compliance without letting management edit the objectives, and table it at the Audit Committee with the annual plan.
checklist.done: an approved scope statement exists naming the rules tested, the inherent risk ratings and the explicit out-of-scope boundary.

checklist.step: Write the audit programme with a test step per rule attribute
actions: Turn each rule attribute into its own test step - principal approval before use, required disclosure elements present, AREF filing within 10 business days of first use, notice generated on the trigger date, delivery evidenced.
For each step, state the evidence that will satisfy it and the evidence that will not; a screenshot of a template is not evidence that a customer received it.
Attach the rule text as it stood during the audit period so a later reader can see what was tested against.
Set the sampling method and size per step in advance so sample sizes cannot be reduced once exceptions appear.
checklist.done: the programme holds one test step per rule attribute with pre-agreed evidence standards and pre-set sample sizes.

checklist.step: Walk the notice lifecycle end to end before testing
actions: Walk one live notice from trigger event through due-date computation, generation, print or email dispatch, delivery confirmation and archive, with the Policy Administration Analyst demonstrating each screen.
Walk one communication template from drafting through principal approval, activation, AREF filing and first use with the Marketing Compliance Analyst.
Note every point where a person can override a system control and treat each as a required test step.
Document the walkthrough with screen references and the names of the staff who demonstrated it.
checklist.done: two documented end-to-end walkthroughs exist with named demonstrators and every manual override point recorded as a test step.

checklist.step: Build the audit population independently of management
actions: Extract the notice population directly from the warehouse rather than accepting a management-prepared list, and record the query used.
Add the print vendor production file and the email service provider send file so notices generated outside the standard path are captured.
Extract the template inventory and the AREF submission log for the year.
Reconcile all three sources and record the reconciling items; sign the population as complete with the extract date and counts.
checklist.done: the population is extracted by Internal Audit from source, reconciled across three independent files and signed as complete.

checklist.step: Select the samples and lock the selection
actions: Stratify by notice type, delivery channel and office of supervisory jurisdiction so no OSJ escapes coverage.
Take 100% of retail communications filed with Advertising Regulation and 100% of notice types with a prior-year finding.
Take a random sample with a recorded seed from the remainder sized to the pre-agreed table, with at least 40 items per major notice type.
Lock the sample list in the audit file before requesting evidence so management cannot influence which items are tested.
checklist.done: the sample is stratified, seeded, locked in the file before evidence requests and covers every OSJ and every prior-finding notice type.

checklist.step: Test content attributes on the customer copy
actions: Retrieve the archived customer copy of each sampled notice - the image actually produced, not the template.

Tick each required element: complaint-filing instructions, firm and FINRA contact details, BrokerCheck reference and hyperlink where applicable, SIPC website address and telephone number on account notices, and the Rule 2211 disclosures on variable product material.
Test Rule 2210(d)(1) content standards on the narrative: balanced presentation, no exaggerated or promissory claims, material qualifications not buried.
Record a pass or fail per attribute per item rather than an overall impression, and attach the annotated copy.
checklist.done: each sampled item carries a per-attribute pass or fail with the annotated customer copy attached.

checklist.step: Test timing attributes against recomputed deadlines
actions: Recompute each sampled notice's due date from the source trigger date using the rule window and the correct calendar, rather than reading the system due date.
Compare the delivery confirmation date to the recomputed due date and record days variance per item.
Recompute the AREF filing deadline as first-use date plus 10 business days and compare to the submission date.
Where the trigger date on the record differs from the underlying event timestamp, use the earlier and record the difference as a finding in its own right.
checklist.done: every sampled item has an independently recomputed deadline, a stated days variance and a note on any shifted trigger date.

checklist.step: Test principal approval and segregation on communications
actions: For each sampled template, confirm the principal approval id, approver name and approval date exist and pre-date the activation timestamp.
Confirm the approver holds the required principal registration by checking their CRD record with the Producer Licensing Coordinator.
Confirm the approver is not the author, and list self-approvals as High-rated findings.
Confirm the version in use matches the version approved by comparing content hashes or, failing that, a page-by-page read.
checklist.done: every sampled template shows a pre-dated approval by a separately registered principal, with the in-use version matching the approved version.

checklist.step: Test the disclosure and routing controls at the offices of supervisory jurisdiction
actions: Select a sample of OSJs and request their Rule 4513 complaint file directly from the branch rather than centrally.
Confirm the file holds each written complaint and the action taken and is retained 4 years.
Confirm the branch uses the current disclosure wording on locally produced correspondence, since local templates are where old wording survives.
Interview the supervising principal on how a written complaint reaches the complaints function and test one live example.
checklist.done: each sampled OSJ produced its own 4-year complaint file, uses current disclosure wording locally and demonstrated a live complaint routing example.

checklist.step: Extrapolate exceptions to the population
actions: Compute the exception rate per attribute and apply it to the stratum population to estimate the number of customers affected.
For content failures traced to a template defect, count the actual sends of that template version rather than extrapolating - the exposure is known exactly.
State the estimate and its basis in the finding so management cannot argue the issue is isolated without evidence.
Have the Chief Audit Executive review every extrapolation before it enters the draft report.
checklist.done: each exception is extrapolated or, where the template is known, exactly quantified, with the basis stated and reviewed.

checklist.step: Rate the findings and agree management actions
actions: Rate each finding High, Medium or Low on customer impact, regulatory consequence and the number of customers affected.
Issue any High finding as an interim memo to the Audit Committee chair and the Head of Compliance immediately rather than holding it for the report.
Agree with the process owner a specific action, a named owner and a date within 90 days of report issue; reject actions phrased as reviews or reminders.
Record management's response verbatim, including any disagreement, and keep the audit rating unchanged where management disputes it.
checklist.done: every finding carries a rating, a specific action with a named owner and a date inside 90 days, and High findings were reported on discovery.

checklist.step: Issue the report and table it at the Audit Committee
actions: Issue the draft to management by 15 October with a 10-business-day response window.
Publish the final report with scope, methodology, sample sizes, findings, ratings, extrapolations, the opinion and management responses.
Table the report at the Q4 Audit Committee with the open action list and the prior-year actions still outstanding.
Record the committee's directions with owners and dates.
checklist.done: the final report is issued after the response window, tabled at the Q4 Audit Committee and the committee's directions are recorded with owners.

checklist.step: Re-test agreed actions before closing them
actions: On each action due date, request the evidence that the fix is live - a configuration export, a corrected template version, a delivery report - not a status update.
Re-test a fresh sample of items processed after the fix date to confirm the control now works in production.
Close the finding only on the re-test result and record the re-test sample and date on the finding.
Escalate any action overdue by more than 30 days to the Audit Committee by owner name.
checklist.done: every closed finding carries a post-fix re-test sample and date, and overdue actions are named to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Run the half-year interim walkthrough
actions: At half-year, re-walk the key automated controls - due-date computation, non-suppressible flags, principal approval gate - and confirm none has been disabled since the audit.
Pull the change records for the in-scope systems for the half-year and confirm each FINRA-affecting change carried a compliance approval.
Test 10 recent notices against their recomputed deadlines as a spot check.
Report the interim result to the Head of Compliance and note it in the audit file as continuous coverage.
checklist.done: a half-year interim walkthrough is documented showing key controls still live, changes approved and a 10-item spot check performed.

checklist.step: Lock and retain the audit file
actions: Complete the reviewer sign-off on every workpaper and clear all review notes before locking.
Lock the file from edit at report issue so the record cannot change after the opinion was given.
Apply 6-year retention and copy the final report to the compliance evidence repository under REG-014-C06.
Confirm the file is retrievable by audit year, rule cite and finding id.
checklist.done: the file is fully signed off, locked at report issue, 6-year retained and retrievable by audit year, rule cite and finding id.

testing.step: Build the verification population of audit coverage
actions: Extract the audit scope statement, the programme test steps, the sample schedules and the finding log for the audit year.
Extract independently from the warehouse the full population of notice types, template versions and OSJs that existed in the year.
Build a coverage matrix of what existed against what the audit actually tested.
Sign the coverage population as complete with the extract date and counts.
testing.done: a coverage matrix exists comparing everything that existed in the year to everything the audit tested, signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the audit population to the source of record
actions: Re-run the audit's population query and compare the row count and totals to the population signed in the audit file.
Confirm the print vendor and email service files were included, since a warehouse-only population misses out-of-band sends.
List every notice type, template version or OSJ present in the source but absent from the audit population as a scope gap.
State the reconciliation in a single calculation in the workpaper.
testing.done: the audit population is re-derived from source and every source item absent from it is listed as a scope gap.

testing.step: Draw a documented re-performance sample from the audit's own sample
actions: Take 100% of items the audit recorded as exceptions, to confirm the exception was real and correctly rated.
Take 100% of items supporting a High-rated finding.
Take 15 items the audit passed, selected at random with a recorded seed, to test whether a pass was justified.
Record the seed, strata and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the re-performance sample covers all audit exceptions, all High-finding support and 15 seeded pass items.

testing.step: Re-perform the content test on the same customer copies
actions: Retrieve the same archived customer copies the audit used, from the repository rather than from the audit file, to confirm the evidence exists at source.
Independently tick each required element and reach a pass or fail without reading the auditor's conclusion.
Compare to the audit's per-attribute result and investigate every difference in both directions - a false pass matters as much as a false fail.
Record the comparison per item in the workpaper.
testing.done: each re-performed item has an independent per-attribute result compared to the audit's, with differences investigated both ways.

testing.step: Recompute the timing tests and the extrapolations
actions: Recompute due dates for the sampled items from source trigger dates and compare to the audit's recomputation, including the holiday calendar used.
Recompute the exception rate per attribute and the population extrapolation, checking the stratum sizes the audit applied.
For template-driven content failures, recount the actual sends of the defective template version and compare to the exposure the audit reported.
Flag any understated exposure as a finding against the audit itself.
testing.done: deadline recomputation and exposure extrapolation are independently reproduced and any understatement is flagged.

testing.step: Verify auditor independence and reviewer sign-off
actions: List every person who performed a test step and check their role history against Compliance, Policy Administration and Marketing for the two prior years.
Confirm no auditor tested a process they previously operated and that the Chief Audit Executive signed the file.
Confirm every workpaper carries a preparer and a reviewer, both dated, and that review notes were cleared before lock.
Confirm the file was locked at report issue and check the audit trail for edits afterwards.
testing.done: auditor independence is evidenced, every workpaper carries dated preparer and reviewer sign-off and no post-lock edits exist.

testing.step: Trace findings through to evidenced remediation
actions: For each closed finding, open the closure evidence and confirm it is a re-test of post-fix items rather than a management assertion.
Confirm the re-test sample was drawn after the fix date and covers the same attribute that failed.
For open findings past their due date, confirm the escalation to the Audit Committee names the owner.
List any finding closed on assertion alone as an exception.
testing.done: every closed finding is supported by a post-fix re-test and every overdue finding shows a named escalation.

testing.step: Check the deadline discipline of the audit cycle itself
actions: Compare actual fieldwork completion to the 30 September milestone and draft issue to the 15 October milestone, recording days variance.
Confirm the management response window was 10 business days and that the final report went to the Q4 Audit Committee.
Confirm every agreed action date falls within 90 days of report issue and list those that do not.
Confirm any High finding was reported to the Audit Committee chair on discovery rather than at report issue.
testing.done: every audit-cycle milestone is compared to actual with days variance stated, and early High-finding reporting is evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception against the audit process itself, carrying the test step, the item id and what the re-performance found.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: scope gap, population incomplete, sample not locked, evidence standard not met, exception missed, exposure understated, finding closed on assertion.
Assign an owner in Internal Audit and a remediation date before the next audit cycle opens.
Carry every open exception into the scoping of the next annual audit as a mandatory coverage item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with the test step and finding, a root cause, an Internal Audit owner, a date and a next-cycle coverage commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the re-performance agreement rate with the audit's conclusions and the count of missed exceptions.
Write the conclusion on whether the annual audit provides reliable assurance over the FINRA notice and communication controls - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed no part of the audit and none of the tested process, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee alongside the audit report and file the signed workpaper under REG-014-C06.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating the re-performance agreement rate, missed exceptions, a conclusion on audit reliability and an Audit Committee reporting date is filed.
