checklist.step: Map the supervisory structure the rules actually require
actions: Read Rule 3110(a) and list each required element: a supervisory system, written procedures, designated registered principals, designated offices of supervisory jurisdiction, an annual compliance meeting and reasonable review of the business.
Map each element to the body or role that discharges it - board, Compliance Committee, Chief Compliance Officer, designated principals - and record any element with no owner.
Add the Rule 3130 requirement for an annual CEO certification supported by a report to the board and audit committee.
Add the Rule 4370 requirement for a board-approved business continuity plan reviewed at least annually and for emergency contact information maintained with FINRA.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the map before it drives any charter change.
checklist.done: a counsel-confirmed map exists showing every Rule 3110/3130/4370 element with a named owning body or role and no unowned elements.

checklist.step: Write the charters to the mapped responsibilities
actions: Draft or update the board and Compliance, Audit and Risk committee charters so each mapped responsibility appears in exactly one charter.
State composition, quorum, meeting frequency, standing agenda items, reporting lines and delegated authorities in each charter.
Write the standing agenda to include the items the rules expect: compliance report, complaint and 4530 reporting summary, supervisory findings, the 3130 report and the annual BCP review.
Circulate to General Counsel for legal review and to the Head of Compliance for regulatory coverage before board approval.
Version each charter and record the approving resolution and date on the front page.
checklist.done: each responsibility sits in exactly one versioned charter, with composition, quorum, standing agenda and the approving resolution recorded.

checklist.step: Approve the charters at the board and record the resolution
actions: Table the charters for annual approval at the first board meeting of the year and record the resolution number, date and vote.
Confirm the meeting met the quorum defined in the constitution before any resolution was taken.
Publish the approved charters to the board portal library and retire the superseded versions to a read-only archive.
Diary the next annual review 12 months out with 60- and 30-day reminders.
checklist.done: charters are approved by a quorate board with a recorded resolution, published to the portal and diarised for review within 12 months.

checklist.step: Maintain the register of designated principals and offices of supervisory jurisdiction
actions: Maintain a register of every supervisory position with the named holder, CRD number, registration category, the branch or OSJ supervised and the effective dates.
Reconcile the register to the CRD branch office record monthly so a location operating as an OSJ is registered as one.
On any departure or role change, name a successor within 30 days and record the interim coverage in the meantime.
Report any position vacant beyond 30 days to the Head of Compliance and the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: the register reconciles monthly to CRD, every position names a holder with CRD number, and vacancies beyond 30 days are escalated.

checklist.step: Assign an owning principal to every written supervisory procedure
actions: Build a WSP ownership map listing each procedure section, the rule it addresses, the owning registered principal and the last review date.
Flag every section with no owner or a review older than 12 months and assign an owner and a review date.
Require each owner to attest annually that the procedure reflects the business as conducted, not as designed.
Report the ownership and currency position to the Compliance Committee each quarter.
checklist.done: every WSP section has a named owning principal, a review inside 12 months and an annual owner attestation.

checklist.step: Run the meeting cycle to the charter
actions: Publish the annual meeting calendar for the board and each committee at the charter frequency and issue notice inside the notice period.
Build each agenda from the charter's standing items plus escalations from the Head of Compliance and the Chief Audit Executive.
Distribute the pack the required number of days before the meeting and record the distribution date.
Record attendance against the membership list at the start of each meeting and confirm quorum on the record before business is taken.
checklist.done: meetings run at charter frequency with the notice period met, standing agenda items covered and quorum confirmed on the record.

checklist.step: Minute the supervisory decisions with enough substance to be evidence
actions: Minute what was presented, what was challenged, what was decided and what was deferred, naming the owner and date for each action.
Record the compliance report, the complaint and 4530 summary and any supervisory failure discussed, since these are what an examiner looks for.
Circulate the draft minutes within 10 business days and approve them at the following meeting with any amendments recorded.
Keep the action log alive between meetings and report overdue actions at the next sitting.
checklist.done: minutes are drafted within 10 business days, capture challenge and decision with owners and dates, and are approved at the following meeting.

checklist.step: Deliver the annual Rule 3130 report and certification
actions: Have the Chief Compliance Officer prepare the report evidencing the firm's processes to establish, maintain, review, test and modify compliance policies and written supervisory procedures.
Hold the required meeting between the CEO and the Chief Compliance Officer and minute the discussion of the compliance processes and any material gaps.
Present the report to the board and the audit committee before the certification is executed, and record the presentation in the minutes.
Execute the annual certification on the same date each year and file the signed certification with the report.
Record every gap identified with an owner and a date and track them like audit findings.
checklist.done: a minuted CEO/CCO meeting, a board and audit committee presentation and a signed annual certification exist, with gaps tracked to owners and dates.

checklist.step: Review and approve the business continuity plan annually
actions: Review the BCP against the Rule 4370 elements: data back-up and recovery, mission-critical systems, financial and operational assessments, alternate communications with customers and employees, alternate physical location, critical business constituent, bank and counter-party impact, regulatory reporting and customer access to funds and securities.
Update the plan for any material change in business, structure, location or technology since the last review.
Test the plan and record the test date, scope, results and remediation actions.
Have the plan approved by a designated member of senior management and table the approval at the board.
Disclose the plan summary to customers as required and publish it on the website.
checklist.done: the BCP is reviewed against every Rule 4370 element, tested with recorded results, approved by senior management and its summary published.

checklist.step: Verify the FINRA emergency contact information after year end
actions: In January, open the FINRA Contact System through FINRA Gateway and review the two emergency contacts, one of whom must be a member of senior management and a registered principal.
Verify or update names, titles, telephone numbers and email addresses and record the verification within 17 business days after the calendar year end.
Update within 30 days at any point in the year when a contact leaves or changes role, rather than waiting for the annual cycle.
Record the verification date and the confirmation in the tracker as the evidence.
checklist.done: the emergency contacts are verified in FINRA Gateway within 17 business days of year end with a recorded confirmation, and mid-year changes updated within 30 days.

checklist.step: Assess structural changes against Rule 1017 before they happen
actions: Require Corporate Development and the business to notify Compliance of any proposed change in ownership, control, business lines, asset transfer or personnel with at least 90 days' notice.
Assess each against Rule 1017 and FINRA By-Laws Article III and record a written determination whether a continuing membership application is required.
Where required, file the application at least 30 days before the change and record the filing date and FINRA correspondence.
Never allow the change to take effect before FINRA approval where approval is required, and record that gate on the project plan.
checklist.done: each structural change carries a written Rule 1017 determination, a filing at least 30 days ahead where required, and a documented go-live gate.

checklist.step: Maintain the delegation of authority framework
actions: Maintain a delegation schedule showing every authority delegated by the board, the delegate, the limits and the reporting-back requirement.
Reconcile the schedule to the system entitlements that actually enforce the limits and raise a gap where a system permits more than the delegation allows.
Re-approve the schedule annually with the charters and on any change of delegate.
Report exercised authorities above a threshold back to the delegating body each quarter.
checklist.done: the delegation schedule is annually re-approved, reconciled to system entitlements and reported back quarterly on above-threshold exercises.

checklist.step: Assess board and committee composition against the charter
actions: Check each committee's membership against its charter for number, independence and required skills, and confirm the chair meets any stated qualification.
Confirm every member's continuing eligibility, including any registration or statutory disqualification check with the Producer Compliance Manager.
Identify vacancies and succession risk and report them to the Nomination process with a target fill date.
Record the composition assessment in the annual governance review.
checklist.done: each committee's composition is assessed against its charter with eligibility confirmed, vacancies reported and the assessment recorded annually.

checklist.step: Escalate and remediate a governance gap
actions: On discovery of a quorum failure, a lapsed charter, an unfilled supervisory designation or a missed certification, open an issue the same week with the exposure period stated.
Determine whether decisions taken during the exposure period require a ratifying resolution and draft it for the next meeting.
Assess with Regulatory Counsel whether the gap is reportable under Rule 4530 or requires disclosure to FINRA.
Assign the structural fix to a named owner with a date and report the gap to the board.
checklist.done: each governance gap has a dated issue with the exposure period, a ratification decision, a 4530 reportability assessment and a board report.

checklist.step: Retain the governance record
actions: Archive charters, agendas, packs, attendance, minutes, resolutions, delegation schedules, designation records, the 3130 report and certification and the BCP review each cycle.
Apply 6-year retention to meeting records and permanent retention to constitutional documents, designations and resolutions.
Confirm records are retrievable by meeting date, committee, resolution number and named principal.
Restrict access to the minute archive to Corporate Secretary, Legal and Compliance and log every access.
checklist.done: the governance record is archived each cycle with correct retention, access-restricted with logged access, and retrievable by meeting, resolution and principal.

testing.step: Build the population of governance bodies, meetings and designations
actions: Extract every board and committee meeting held in the period with date, body, attendance and minute reference.
Extract the charter library with version and approval dates, the delegation schedule and the register of designated principals and OSJs.
Add the 3130 certification record, the BCP review record and the FINRA emergency contact verification evidence.
Sign the population as complete after reconciling the meeting count to the charter-mandated frequency for each body.
testing.done: a complete population of meetings, charters, designations and annual records exists, reconciled to charter-mandated meeting frequency.

testing.step: Reconcile designations to the regulator's own record
actions: Compare the internal register of designated principals and OSJs to the CRD branch office and registered-person records, line by line.
List any person designated internally without the required principal registration on CRD, and any branch operating as an OSJ but not registered as one.
Confirm the two FINRA emergency contacts on record match the people the firm believes are appointed, including that one is a senior management member and registered principal.
Record every difference with the date it arose and the exposure period.
testing.done: the internal designation register reconciles to CRD and the FINRA contact record, with every difference dated and its exposure period stated.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of meetings and structures
actions: Take 100% of meetings where a compliance or supervisory failure was on the agenda, and 100% of meetings where a charter, delegation or designation changed.
Take 100% of supervisory positions that changed holder in the period.
Take 8 further meetings at random with a recorded seed across the bodies, minimum 15 meetings overall.
Record the seed, strata, population sizes and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all compliance-failure and change meetings and all changed supervisory positions, reproducible from the recorded seed.

testing.step: Recompute quorum and notice for each sampled meeting
actions: Read the quorum requirement from the charter version in force on the meeting date, not the current version.
Count the members actually present from the attendance record, excluding attendees who are not members, and compare to the requirement.
Recompute the notice period as meeting date minus the pack distribution date and compare to the charter requirement.
Treat any resolution taken at an inquorate meeting as an exception requiring ratification, and record which resolutions are affected.
testing.done: quorum and notice are recomputed against the charter version in force for each sampled meeting, with affected resolutions listed.

testing.step: Test charter currency and responsibility coverage
actions: Check each charter's last approval date and flag any beyond 12 months.
Take the Rule 3110/3130/4370 responsibility map and confirm each element appears in exactly one charter - list both unowned elements and elements owned twice.
Confirm the standing agenda items in the charter actually appeared on the agendas held during the year, meeting by meeting.
List any standing item omitted from more than one meeting as a control failure.
testing.done: charter currency is checked, every rule element traces to exactly one charter, and standing agenda coverage is tested meeting by meeting.

testing.step: Re-perform the Rule 3130 certification chain
actions: Open the signed certification and confirm the execution date, the signatory and that it was executed annually without a gap year.
Trace back to the minuted CEO and Chief Compliance Officer meeting and read what was discussed rather than accepting that it occurred.
Confirm the supporting report was presented to both the board and the audit committee before the certification date, evidenced in the minutes.
Confirm every gap identified in the report has an owner, a date and evidenced progress.
testing.done: the certification, the minuted CEO/CCO meeting and the pre-certification board and audit committee presentations are traced in the right order with gaps tracked.

testing.step: Test the business continuity plan against Rule 4370
actions: Read the current plan against each Rule 4370 element and mark present or absent element by element rather than as a whole.
Confirm the annual review date is inside 12 months of the prior review and that the plan was updated for the material business changes of the year.
Trace the recorded test to its results and remediation actions, and check the actions closed.
Confirm the plan summary is published and the disclosure to customers made as required, by viewing the live page.
testing.done: every Rule 4370 element is marked present or absent, the annual review and test are evidenced, and the published summary is viewed live.

testing.step: Test supervisory coverage and WSP ownership
actions: For each supervisory position that changed holder, compute the days the position was vacant or covered on an interim basis and flag any beyond 30 days.
Take the WSP ownership map and list every section with no owning principal or a review older than 12 months.
For 10 WSP sections, confirm the named owner is a registered principal and that they completed the annual attestation.
Test two sections against how the business actually operates by interviewing the process owner - a procedure that describes work no one does is a finding.
testing.done: vacancy days are computed per position, WSP ownership and currency are listed, and two sections are tested against actual practice.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the body or position, the exposure period in days and the rule at risk.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: charter review lapsed, quorum not checked before business, designation not backfilled, WSP section unowned, certification chain out of sequence, BCP element missing, contact verification late.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and determine with General Counsel whether ratifying resolutions or a Rule 4530 report are required.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with the exposure period, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a ratification and reportability decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the count of inquorate meetings, lapsed charters, unowned WSP sections and vacancy days against the zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the quorum recomputation, the designation reconciliation and the certification chain.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside the Corporate Secretary's office and drafted no sampled charter or minute, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the board and the Audit Committee at the next sitting and file the signed workpaper under REG-014-C07.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the exception counts, a stated conclusion and dated board and Audit Committee reporting is filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Build the inventory of governance filings with triggers and deadlines
actions: List every governance filing the firm owes: Form BD and its schedules, the annual FINRA entitlement certification, Rule 1017 continuing membership applications, the Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure and the holding-company registration statement.
For each, record the regulator, the submission channel (FINRA Gateway, the lead state's electronic filing portal), the trigger, the deadline, the preparer, the reviewer and the certifying officer.

Record the specific data items each form demands - direct owners and percentages, executive officers and titles, control persons, business lines, office locations, disciplinary disclosures - and where each comes from.
Have General Counsel confirm the inventory is complete against the entity's registrations before it drives the calendar.
checklist.done: a counsel-confirmed inventory exists naming regulator, channel, trigger, deadline, roles and the data items and sources for every governance filing.

checklist.step: Load the inventory into a live filing calendar
actions: Create a calendar entry per dated filing with the statutory date, an internal target 10 business days earlier and the named preparer, reviewer and certifier.
Set the CGAD entry to 1 June and the entitlement certification to its annual window; set Form BD entries to open on a trigger rather than a date.
Configure alerts at T-45, T-30, T-14 and T-3 days to the preparer and the reviewer, with escalation to General Counsel at T-3.
Review the calendar monthly with Legal and Compliance and record the review.
checklist.done: every dated filing has a calendar entry with an internal target, named roles, four alert points and a recorded monthly review.

checklist.step: Detect the events that trigger a Form BD amendment
actions: Read every board and committee minute and every officer appointment or resignation letter within 5 business days of approval.

Screen each against the Form BD amendable items: direct owners and their percentages, executive officers, control persons, business name and address, office locations, business activities and disciplinary events.
Open a filing task the day a triggering change is minuted, with the 30-day clock running from the change date, not the minute-approval date.
Record a written no-filing determination where a change is screened out, so the screening decision is itself evidenced.
checklist.done: every minuted governance change is screened within 5 business days and produces either a filing task with a 30-day clock or a written no-filing determination.

checklist.step: Assess material business changes against Rule 1017 before commitment
actions: Require Corporate Development to notify Legal and Compliance of any proposed merger, acquisition, asset transfer, change of control, new business line or material personnel change with 90 days' notice.
Assess the proposal against the Rule 1017 triggers and record a written determination with the reasoning and the rule cite.
Where an application is required, file it at least 30 days before the intended change and set a project gate that blocks effect until FINRA approval.
Manage FINRA's information requests through a single point of contact and log every request, response and due date.
Update the project plan whenever the review timeline moves, so the business never assumes an approval date.
checklist.done: each material change carries a written Rule 1017 determination, an application filed at least 30 days ahead where required, and a blocking go-live gate.

checklist.step: Gather and verify the data behind each filing
actions: Pull direct owners and percentages from the share register, executive officers and titles from the board resolutions, and office locations from the property and branch registers.
Reconcile each figure to its source document and attach the source to the working paper - a filed ownership percentage must trace to the register, not to last year's form.
Query any difference with the source owner and resolve it before drafting rather than filing with a caveat.
Record the as-at date of every data item so the filing states facts as at a defined date.
checklist.done: every filed data item traces to an attached source document with a stated as-at date and no unresolved differences.

checklist.step: Draft the Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure
actions: Draft the CGAD to the lead state's required content: the corporate governance framework and structure, board and committee composition and qualifications, the policies and practices of the board, and management oversight including succession planning and compensation practices.
State the level at which the disclosure is made - ultimate controlling person, intermediate holding company or insurer - and keep it consistent with the prior year or explain the change.
Cross-check every assertion against the charters, minutes and delegation schedule so the document describes the governance that actually operates.
Have General Counsel review for accuracy and confidentiality handling, since CGAD material is filed under the state's confidentiality protections.
checklist.done: a CGAD draft exists covering framework, board composition, policies and management oversight, cross-checked to charters and minutes and reviewed by General Counsel.

checklist.step: Run the review and officer certification before submission
actions: Review the draft against the form instructions item by item and record the review as a completed checklist rather than an email approval.
Confirm the preparer and the reviewer are different people and that neither is the certifying officer.
Route to the certifying officer with the supporting schedules attached so the certification is informed rather than nominal.
Capture the signed certification with its date and store it with the working papers.
checklist.done: an item-by-item review checklist, separated preparer and reviewer, and a dated signed officer certification exist before submission.

checklist.step: Submit through the regulator's own channel and capture the acknowledgement
actions: Submit Form BD amendments and the entitlement certification through FINRA Gateway using the firm's entitled user, and the CGAD through the lead state's filing channel.
Complete every mandatory field, attach the schedules and run the system validation before pressing submit.
Capture the submission id, timestamp and the confirmation or acknowledgement, and download the as-filed PDF the same day.
Attach the as-filed PDF and acknowledgement to the calendar entry and set its status to Filed only on the acknowledgement, not on the send.
checklist.done: each filing has a submission id, a timestamp, an acknowledgement and an as-filed PDF attached, with status set on the acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Complete the annual FINRA entitlement certification
actions: Extract the list of the firm's FINRA Gateway users with their entitlements and compare it to current employment and role from the HR feed.
Remove entitlements for leavers and role changers before certifying, since certifying a stale list is itself the failure.
Have the designated Super Account Administrator complete the certification inside the annual window and record the completion date.
File the certified user list with the date and the administrator's name as the evidence.
checklist.done: the Gateway entitlement list is reconciled to HR, stale access removed, and the annual certification completed and dated inside the window.

checklist.step: Handle regulator questions and deficiency notices
actions: Log every regulator question, comment or deficiency notice on the filing record the day it arrives with its own response deadline.
Draft the response with the source evidence attached and have General Counsel clear it before it is sent.
Where the regulator identifies an inaccuracy, file the corrective amendment rather than answering the question and leaving the record wrong.
Close the item only on the regulator's confirmation and record the closure date.
checklist.done: every regulator communication is logged with a deadline, answered with counsel clearance, corrected by amendment where needed and closed on confirmation.

checklist.step: Amend promptly when a filed fact changes or proves wrong
actions: Re-screen every filed fact quarterly against the share register, officer list and branch register to catch drift between events.
On any difference, open an amendment task the same day with the 30-day clock running from the date the fact changed.
Where the original filing was wrong rather than out of date, record the cause and notify General Counsel, since an inaccurate filing carries its own consequence.
File the amendment and record the new submission id against the original filing record.
checklist.done: the quarterly re-screen runs, every difference opens a same-day amendment task, and amendments are linked to the original filing record.

checklist.step: Report the filing position to the board
actions: Table a filing status paper at each board meeting listing filings made in the period with dates, filings due before the next meeting and any late or amended filing.
Report every open Rule 1017 application with its status and the go-live gate it holds.
Report the CGAD submission and any lead-state follow-up.
Record the board's directions with owners and dates.
checklist.done: a filing status paper is tabled each meeting covering filings made, due, late and amended, with recorded board directions.

checklist.step: Reconcile the filing log to the legal entity register
actions: Take the legal entity register - officers, directors, owners, registered addresses, business activities - and compare it to what stands filed on Form BD.
List every difference with the date the underlying change took effect and the days elapsed since.
Give each difference an owner and a filing decision within 5 business days.
Publish the difference count monthly so drift between the register and the filed record is visible.
checklist.done: the register and the filed record are reconciled with every difference dated, owned and decided within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Escalate and remediate a missed or inaccurate filing
actions: On any missed deadline or discovered inaccuracy, open an issue the same day recording the filing, the days late or the incorrect fact and the period the record was wrong.
File the late or corrective submission immediately with an explanatory cover where the channel allows one.
Assess with Regulatory Counsel whether the failure requires a Rule 4530 report or a disclosure to the lead state.
Assign the process fix to a named owner with a date and report the failure to the board at its next meeting.
checklist.done: each missed or inaccurate filing has a same-day issue, an immediate corrective submission, a reportability assessment and a board report.

checklist.step: Retain the filing evidence
actions: Archive per filing: the as-filed PDF, the working papers with source documents, the review checklist, the officer certification, the submission id and the acknowledgement.
Apply 6-year retention and permanent retention to the resolutions and constitutional documents relied on.
Confirm retrieval by filing type, regulator, submission id and filing date.
Restrict access to CGAD material in line with the lead state's confidentiality protections and log every access.
checklist.done: each filing is archived complete with source and acknowledgement, correctly retained, retrievable by submission id and access-restricted for CGAD material.

testing.step: Build the population of filing-triggering events independently
actions: Extract every board and committee minute, officer appointment and resignation, share transfer and branch opening or closure in the period from the primary records, not from the filing log.
Add the legal entity register as at the start and end of the period and diff it to surface changes no one minuted.
Add the dated filings due in the period from the filing inventory.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date, event count and the reconciling items.
testing.done: an event population built from minutes and the entity register diff, plus the dated filings due, is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile events to filings made
actions: Match each triggering event to a filing or to a written no-filing determination and list unmatched events as automatic exceptions.
Match each dated filing in the inventory to a submission id and acknowledgement, listing any due filing with no submission.
Match every submission back to a triggering event or a calendar entry so a filing made without a driver is also inspected.
State the three-way reconciliation as a single calculation in the workpaper.
testing.done: events, filings and acknowledgements reconcile three ways with every unmatched item raised as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample across filing types
actions: Take 100% of Rule 1017 applications, 100% of amendments filed after a discovered inaccuracy and 100% of ownership or control changes.
Take the CGAD and the annual entitlement certification in full.
Take 10 further Form BD amendments at random with a recorded seed, minimum 20 filings overall.
Record the seed, strata, population sizes and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all 1017 applications, control changes, corrective amendments, the CGAD and the certification, reproducible from the seed.

testing.step: Recompute every deadline from the underlying change date
actions: For each sampled event-driven filing, take the change date from the resolution or transfer document, not the filing record, and add 30 days.
Compare to the submission timestamp on the acknowledgement and record days late per item.
For the CGAD, compare the submission date to 1 June; for Rule 1017, confirm the application pre-dates the change by at least 30 days and that approval pre-dates effect.
Attach the calculation and the source date evidence to the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled deadline is recomputed from the underlying change document with days late stated and the 1017 approval-before-effect test performed.

testing.step: Re-perform the accuracy of filed facts against source
actions: Open the as-filed PDF for each sampled filing and take the key facts: direct owners and percentages, executive officers and titles, control persons, office locations and business activities.
Trace each fact to the share register, the appointing resolution or the branch register as at the filing's stated as-at date.
Treat any difference as a fail on accuracy even where the filing was timely, and quantify how long the record stood wrong.
Record fact-by-fact agreement in the workpaper rather than an overall conclusion.
testing.done: each sampled filing has a fact-by-fact trace to source with differences quantified by the period the record stood wrong.

testing.step: Verify review, certification and segregation
actions: Confirm the item-by-item review checklist exists and is dated before submission.
Confirm the preparer, the reviewer and the certifying officer are three different people.
Confirm the signed officer certification is dated on or before the submission timestamp; a certification dated afterwards is an exception equal to none at all.
Confirm the supporting schedules attached to the certification are the ones actually filed.
testing.done: every sampled filing shows a pre-dated review checklist, three separate people and a certification dated no later than submission.

testing.step: Re-perform the CGAD content against the governance that operates
actions: Take the CGAD's assertions on board and committee composition, meeting frequency, qualifications and oversight practices.
Trace each assertion to the charters in force, the attendance records and the minutes for the year covered.
List any assertion the underlying records do not support, since an inaccurate CGAD is a governance failure in its own right.
Confirm the disclosure level and any change from the prior year is explained.
testing.done: every CGAD assertion is traced to charters, attendance and minutes, with unsupported assertions listed and the disclosure level confirmed.

testing.step: Test the entitlement certification against actual access
actions: Extract the FINRA Gateway user list certified during the annual window and compare it to the HR record of employment and role at the certification date.
List any certified user who had left or changed role before the certification date as an exception.
Confirm removals identified during the certification were actually executed in the access system, with dates.
Check for Gateway activity by a removed user after their removal date.
testing.done: the certified user list agrees to HR at the certification date, removals are evidenced as executed and no post-removal activity is unexplained.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the filing type, regulator, the days late or the incorrect fact and the period the record stood wrong.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: change not screened, clock started from the wrong date, data taken from the prior filing rather than source, certification obtained late, 1017 assessment missed, entitlement list not reconciled.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and decide with Regulatory Counsel whether a corrective amendment, a Rule 4530 report or a lead-state notification is required.
Carry every open exception into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with days late or the wrong fact, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a corrective-filing decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the on-time filing rate, the count of inaccurate filed facts and the count of changes effected before a required approval, against the 100% thresholds.
